free.name: Pixellot
free.hq: Israel, with US offices in Atlanta and Durham
free.payer_model_label: Platform pays for cameras and shares revenue
free.one_line: Pixellot builds fixed multi-sensor cameras (Show S3) and a portable one (Air NXT) that produce and stream matches unattended, and sells the output through platform partners such as PlayOn in US high schools and through a direct Pixellot You shop for clubs [pix-04, pix-02, pix-06].
free.who_for: Federations, leagues, school networks and streaming platforms that want hundreds of venues producing live games with graphics and ads and a revenue share on the audience, plus clubs that buy an Air NXT and a Team or Club plan for their own coaching video [pix-01, pix-05]. Football clubs in Italy get the Air NXT at 999 euros with plans from 1,009 euros per year, and professional academies such as Fiorentina have used the fixed system across a whole training centre [pix-05, pix-10].
free.why: Pixellot exists because live production of youth sport only pays when a camera costs less than one camera operator per season, and its fixed systems in 9,000 US schools proved that model at scale [pix-01]. It matters now because the November 2025 PlayOn extension and the January 2026 35 million dollar raise moved the company from selling cameras to sharing revenue on the content the cameras generate, which it calls AI as a Service [pix-02, pix-01]. That tells you where the space is going, with capture becoming a cost line inside a media business and the vendor's income tied to viewership and monetisation, with hardware reduced to an enabler [pix-21].
free.price_band: Pixellot You direct shop: Air NXT €999 plus €1,009 (Team) or €1,299 (Club) per year in the EU price list; fixed Show systems and partner deployments are quote-only or revenue-share

italy.note: Fiorentina chose Pixellot for nine pitches at its new training centre in June 2022 and the Lega Nazionale Dilettanti streamed all 114 group matches of the 2023 Torneo delle Regioni with Pixellot technology, while the Pixellot You shop routes Italian demo requests to a local reseller calendar and offers an Italian-language storefront [pix-10, pix-11, pix-05].

free.evidence_note: Direct-to-club prices come from the price tables embedded in the Pixellot You site script for EU, US and UK markets, and corporate claims from Pixellot press releases; the company is private with no published accounts, fixed-system pricing is quote-only, and reviewer volume is small, so several judgements rest on vendor statements and trade press.

verdict.look_if: You are a league, federation, school network or streaming platform that wants unattended live production with graphics, ads and commentary across many venues and is prepared to negotiate a revenue share or per-venue contract [pix-01, pix-09]. You are a club that wants one portable camera for coaching video on a published EU price list and values 12 months of storage and unlimited events on the Club plan [pix-05, pix-06].
verdict.skip_if: You want published fixed-system pricing, a European data residency statement or a downloadable master file from the consumer app, because Pixellot publishes none of these and app reviewers report that the app shares links and offers no file export [pix-15, pix-17]. You want a vendor with a large public base of coach reviews, since the Pixellot You app has 16 ratings on iOS and 58 on Google Play [pix-17, pix-18].
watch_outs: The Pixellot You terms grant Pixellot a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, sublicensable licence to use, distribute and modify your content, and state that Pixellot has no obligation to store it [pix-16].

Pixellot processes tracking and video data as processor and requires the customer to obtain parental consent for athletes under 18, so the club carries the consent duty and Pixellot offers an opt-out from facial recognition and no blurring [pix-15].
The privacy policy names Israel as the processing country and relies on standard contractual clauses for EEA transfers, with no named cloud region for European footage [pix-15].

Pixellot You prices are loaded from a script file whose version stamp dates from March 2025, and the EU plans page itself returned a 404 during verification, so treat the EUR figures as list prices to be confirmed at checkout [pix-05, pix-06].

Live streaming on the Air NXT is described on the US plans page as coming soon and available in a limited partner release, so a club buying the portable camera for live output should get that in writing [pix-06].
Fixed Show systems and partner deployments have no public price, and the AIaaS model ties the vendor's revenue to viewership, which shapes what gets built for coaches versus fans [pix-21, pix-02].

criteria.use_case_fit: Pixellot covers 19 sports with sport-specific algorithms and sells two distinct things, a fixed Show S3 system for venues that need live production with graphics, ads and commentary, and a portable Air NXT with a Team or Club plan for coaching video [pix-04, pix-09, pix-06]. The company's volume sits in US high schools, with 16,000 systems in 9,000 schools streaming more than 500,000 events per year through PlayOn [pix-01, pix-02]. Football deployments range from the Fiorentina training centre to LND tournament streaming in Italy [pix-10, pix-11].
criteria.capture_quality: The Air NXT carries a dual 4K 12 megapixel array, a six-hour battery with USB-C charging, up to 512 gigabytes of storage for around 32 hours of video, stereo audio and a weight under two kilograms [pix-07, pix-08]. It outputs a broadcast view, a full panorama and a tactical view for coaches [pix-07]. The fixed Show system is a panoramic multi-camera unit that adjusts to poor lighting and adds embedded graphics and audio inputs for commentary [pix-09].
criteria.automation_accuracy: Pixellot publishes no tracking accuracy figures and describes the production as fully automated with sport-specific AI calibration across 19 sports [pix-09]. The company added automated first down markers and replays for American football during the PlayOn partnership, which shows the production automation going beyond a follow-cam [pix-02]. Reviewer commentary on tracking quality is thin, with the Pixellot You app praised for video quality and criticised for playback freezes, with tracking errors absent from the complaints [pix-17, pix-18].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: The Show system stitches a panoramic view from multiple sensors and DoublePlay adds automated multi-camera production for baseball and softball [pix-04, pix-09]. The Air NXT stitches its two 4K sensors into one panorama and offers no second unit synchronisation in the public material [pix-07, pix-08]. Third-party camera ingestion is not described for either product [pix-09].
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live production is the core of the fixed system, which streams live and on demand with rewind, embedded graphics and ad formats over 3G or 4G connections [pix-09]. Live streaming on the Air was announced in September 2022 over cellular modem, Ethernet or Wi-Fi, yet the current US plans page still lists live streaming on the Air as coming soon and limited to a partner release [pix-22, pix-06]. No latency figures are published [pix-09].
criteria.reliability_resilience: Pixellot reports 2.5 million production hours in 2025 and an average above 100,000 events per month, which is the strongest volume evidence in this database for unattended production [pix-01]. The Pixellot You Android app is criticised for freezing during playback and the iOS app for missing iPad support, while the fixed system carries no public reliability data beyond the partner numbers [pix-18, pix-17]. The B&H listing gives the Air NXT a one-year limited warranty [pix-07].
criteria.portability_install: The Air NXT ships in a waterproof case, weighs under two kilograms and runs six hours on battery or longer from a power bank [pix-07, pix-08]. The Show S3 is a fixed installation for gyms and stadiums and Pixellot publishes no installation guide or cost for it, with partner programmes handling deployment in schools [pix-09, pix-02]. A GoPro-based entry option exists in the US shop for indoor sports [pix-06].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: The Air NXT uploads over Wi-Fi or 4G and 5G, and mobile uploads run through the Pixellot Control app [pix-07, pix-06]. The Show system is described as working on low bandwidth 3G or 4G links for live output [pix-09]. Pixellot publishes no minimum upload speed for either product [pix-08].
criteria.workflow_ux: The Pixellot You app gives clip creation, sharing links and a video player, and the plan includes VidSwap coaching analysis tools and one free automated game breakdown [pix-06]. App reviewers score it 3.9 on iOS from 16 ratings and 4.0 on Google Play from 58, praising quality and editing and complaining about mandatory fade transitions, no casting to TVs and export that shares links with no file download [pix-17, pix-18]. The storefront and app are available in Italian, German, Spanish and French [pix-06].
criteria.analysis_layer: Analysis runs through VidSwap, acquired in 2019, which offers game breakdowns priced at 55 dollars each in the US bundles, with six free on a one-year plan and twelve on a two-year plan [pix-14, pix-06]. Pixellot Analytics Pro access valued at 500 dollars is bundled with the Air plans [pix-06]. Tactical full-pitch view and tagging inside the Pixellot application are included on the Air [pix-08].
criteria.integrations: Pixellot states it delivers functionality through APIs and SDKs and integrated Helios wearables for automated hockey shift video in April 2026 [pix-20]. GameChanger integrated Pixellot fixed cameras with QR activation in December 2025, and the Air page says footage can be uploaded to external platforms and third-party breakdown tools [pix-19, pix-08]. No public API documentation was found during verification [pix-20].
criteria.distribution_ott: Pixellot OTT is a white-label streaming platform for engagement and monetisation, and the company claims 100 million views of live events streamed [pix-04, pix-01]. Distribution in the US runs through PlayOn's NFHS Network on a five-year revenue-share extension signed in November 2025 [pix-02]. In Italy the 2023 Torneo delle Regioni was streamed with Pixellot technology in collaboration with the regional broadcaster Ideawebtv [pix-11].
criteria.data_access_ownership: The Pixellot You terms state that Pixellot claims no ownership of user content while taking a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence to use, distribute and modify it, and that Pixellot has no obligation to store content and may delete it on termination [pix-16]. Plans include 12 months of storage [pix-06]. App reviewers report that the consumer app only shares links and does not export files, and Pixellot publishes no download policy for the panorama master [pix-17].
criteria.privacy_compliance: Pixellot acts as processor for tracking and video coverage data on behalf of the customer, requires parental consent for athletes under 18, names a data protection officer and relies on standard contractual clauses for EEA transfers, with Israel as the processing country and no named hosting region [pix-15]. Customers can opt out of the facial recognition feature, and no blurring or on-pitch opt-out mechanism is described [pix-15]. The policy was last updated on 19 March 2024 [pix-15].
criteria.security: Pixellot states that it implements physical, technical and administrative measures in line with industry standards and names no certification such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001 in its policy [pix-15]. No security page, status page or penetration test statement was found during verification [pix-15]. Not assessable beyond this from public sources.
criteria.pricing_tco: In the EU list a club pays 999 euros for the Air NXT and 1,009 euros per year for the Team plan or 1,299 euros for the Club plan with unlimited teams, so first-year cost is about 2,008 to 2,298 euros before VAT [pix-05]. Monthly billing runs 109 euros for Team and 139 for Club, and the US shop offers two-year terms at 1,899 and 2,477 dollars with a free Air camera on yearly subscriptions promoted on the page [pix-05, pix-06]. Fixed Show systems and federation deployments are quote-only, and press coverage of the AIaaS model indicates no upfront camera cost for partners in exchange for a revenue share [pix-01, pix-21].
criteria.support_service: Pixellot You plans include free email and chat support, with a Zoho desk widget on the storefront and regional demo calendars by US region and by country [pix-06, pix-05]. No response time targets, SLAs or warranty terms beyond the one-year limited warranty in the B&H listing are published [pix-07]. App reviewers describe support as responsive in getting cameras shipped [pix-17].
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Pixellot raised 161 million dollars in 2022 at a 500 million dollar valuation led by PSG Equity, then 35 million dollars in January 2026 as 15 million equity from PSG and 20 million venture debt [pix-12, pix-01]. Doron Gerstel, former Perion CEO, replaced founder-era CEO Alon Werber in November 2024 when the company had around 200 employees, and the strategy since then centres on AIaaS revenue sharing, personalisation and monetisation [pix-13, pix-21]. The press release feed shows no product or partnership announcement between April and September 2026 [pix-03].
criteria.evidence_references: Fiorentina selected Pixellot in June 2022 for nine pitches with live streaming, analytics and highlights across the academy, women's and men's teams [pix-10]. The Lega Nazionale Dilettanti used Pixellot as technology partner to stream all 114 group matches of the 59th Torneo delle Regioni in April 2023 [pix-11]. The homepage lists Real Sociedad, Benfica, the Scottish Premiership and Grupo Globo among partners, and PlayOn reports 3.4 million high school events produced with Pixellot [pix-04, pix-02]. Italian trade press in August 2026 lists the Air NXT among the reference football cameras and notes that it requires a custom quote [pix-23].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Public coach feedback is limited to 16 iOS ratings at 3.9 and 58 Google Play reviews at 4.0 for the Pixellot You app [pix-17, pix-18]. Positive comments cite video quality and editing, negative ones cite playback freezes, no iPad version, no casting and export limited to links [pix-17, pix-18]. Not assessable at statistical scale from public sources.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: The Air NXT records locally to up to 512 gigabytes and uploads afterwards, while the fixed Show system produces live in an automated workflow that Pixellot describes as delivering footage without human intervention [pix-07, pix-09]. Pixellot describes the Helios integration as processing in the cloud the moment the game hits it [pix-20]. The split of AI work between the camera and the cloud is not documented publicly [pix-09].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The Pixellot You storefront and demo flow run in English, German, Spanish, Mexican Spanish, French and Italian, with country-specific demo calendars for Italy, Germany, France, the UK, Australia, Mexico and Canada [pix-06, pix-05]. Pixellot has offices in Israel, Atlanta and Durham and appointed a chief commercial officer for Australia and New Zealand in December 2025 [pix-14, pix-24].
criteria.upgrade_path: A club can start with the Air NXT on a Team plan, move to the Club plan with unlimited teams and sports, and add VidSwap breakdowns per game [pix-06]. Venues that need live production with graphics move to the fixed Show S3 and Pixellot OTT, which are sold through partners or direct quotes [pix-09, pix-04]. DoublePlay covers baseball and softball with multi-camera production for organisations that expand beyond football [pix-04].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the Show S3 live output with graphics and commentary on a real match against your bandwidth, because low-bandwidth live production is the claim that separates Pixellot from portable rivals [pix-09]. Test the Air NXT tactical view and panorama export for your analysts, since the consumer app is criticised for link-only sharing [pix-08, pix-17]. Ask for the AIaaS terms in writing, including who owns the audience data and the ad inventory [pix-21, pix-02].

free.name: Sportway (incl. MyGame)
free.payer_model_label: Platform pays for cameras and shares revenue
free.one_line: Sportway installs fixed AI cameras in arenas and on pitches at its own cost, produces every match automatically and distributes it through federation branded OTT platforms and consumer services such as MyGame in Norway [sportway-03, sportway-04, sportway-11].
free.who_for: Federations, leagues and media groups that want a whole tier of sport filmed and monetised without asking clubs to buy anything, plus the clubs inside those deals that receive cameras, coaching tools and a revenue share for free [sportway-06, sportway-11, sportway-12]. Individual clubs outside a federation agreement have no public way to buy in.
free.why: Sportway exists because Nordic ice hockey and handball federations wanted every game on a screen and no club would pay for a camera, so the company took on the capital cost and built a rights and subscription business around it, reaching about 2,500 cameras in 21 countries and 250,000 events a year by June 2026 [sportway-01]. It matters now because the June 2026 EUR 20 million round led by Giorgio Chiellini's Gamma Waves, the Studio Automated acquisition and the KNHB ClubhockeyTV deal show the model exporting beyond Scandinavia and into football adjacent sports [sportway-01, sportway-11, sportway-15]. It tells you the grassroots video market is splitting into a consumer camera business and a rights infrastructure business, and Sportway is the clearest European example of the second, with the Norwegian consent fights around MyGame as the cautionary tale [sportway-08, sportway-09].
free.price_band: Clubs pay nothing for cameras or installation under federation deals; consumers pay NOK 139/month or NOK 1,199/year for MyGame in Norway with 20% returned to a chosen club; Playsite and federation platform fees are not public

italy.note: Sportway has a Milan operating base and a partnership with the Italian Ice Sports Federation (FISG) since autumn 2023 covering about 35 ice venues in ice hockey, figure skating, speed skating and curling, with a stated aim to expand beyond ice sports [sportway-02].

free.evidence_note: Consumer pricing, federation deals, funding and company registry data come from primary sources; camera hardware specifications, club level commercial terms and consolidated financials are not public, and privacy history relies on Norwegian press.

verdict.look_if: You run a federation, league or regional media group and want an operator that will fund, install and run cameras across dozens or hundreds of venues in exchange for rights and a subscription model [sportway-01, sportway-11]. You are a club inside one of those agreements and want to understand what you get, which is free capture, a Team Account for tagging and a Player Account for clips, plus a possible revenue share [sportway-06, sportway-14].
verdict.skip_if: You are a single club or academy that wants to buy a camera this month, because Sportway publishes no per club price and works through federation and league agreements [sportway-03, sportway-14]. You need a portable camera for away games and tournaments, since the system is a fixed installation wired to mains and network [sportway-16, sportway-12].
watch_outs: MyGame's Norwegian rollout was paused by Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim and Tromsø municipalities in early 2023 and the Norwegian Data Protection Authority said streaming of children's sport would be hard to do lawfully under the then current setup, so any deployment involving under 18s needs a consent design agreed with the local regulator first [sportway-08, sportway-09].

In December 2022 people were filmed at handball and volleyball training without their knowledge because cameras stayed active outside scheduled matches, which is a design risk of always installed cameras [sportway-10].

The parent company Sportway Media Group AB reported revenue of SEK 756 thousand and a loss after financial items of SEK 14.2 million for 2024 at holding level, and consolidated group accounts are not visible in the free registry view, so scale claims cannot be cross checked against audited numbers [sportway-17].

The camera hardware is described only in general terms as multi lens security grade cameras with proprietary AI, so resolution, frame rate and tracking behaviour must be checked on a live stream in your sport before signing [sportway-16].
Club revenue share is documented for MyGame in Norway at 20% of subscription revenue, and no comparable figure is published for ClubhockeyTV or other markets [sportway-06, sportway-12].

criteria.use_case_fit: Sportway is built for a federation or league that wants every match in a competition tier filmed and distributed, and it fits clubs only as beneficiaries of such a deal [sportway-11, sportway-12]. The company reports 200,000 ice hockey matches a year, 2,000 football matches a season and 20,000 matches across floorball, handball and volleyball, so football is a minority sport in its portfolio today [sportway-03]. Coaching and player tools exist as Team Account and Player Account layers on top of the broadcast feed [sportway-14].
criteria.capture_quality: MyGame describes multi camera, multi lens rigs that film the whole playing area and let the AI frame a 16:9 broadcast picture, with security grade cameras chosen for the job [sportway-16]. Sportway does not publish resolution or frame rate for its fixed cameras, and the Studio Automated acquisition adds AI controlled PTZ cameras for higher production tiers [sportway-15]. Judge the output from a live ClubhockeyTV or MyGame stream in your sport, since no spec sheet exists [sportway-12].
criteria.automation_accuracy: The AI locates the ball or puck, detects active players and the playing surface, and frames the shot following manual camera operator principles, with 5 to 25 matches of training footage per sport and venue type [sportway-16]. Since April 2026 Sportway owns Studio Automated's real time event detection, which generates highlights, clips and replays during matches [sportway-15]. No independent accuracy measurement is public.
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Rigs combine several cameras and lenses to cover the whole field, and the AI selects the framing from that panorama [sportway-16]. Studio Automated adds multicamera automation for remote production in football, ice hockey, basketball and handball [sportway-15]. Details of stitching resolution or the number of virtual angles offered to viewers are not published.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: The whole business is live first, with matches streamed to federation platforms and to TV 2 Play in Norway [sportway-04, sportway-14]. Sportway sells a low latency feed with glass to glass delay under five seconds for betting and data partners [sportway-14]. Standard viewer latency is not published.
criteria.reliability_resilience: The system runs about 2,500 cameras across 21 countries and 250,000 events a year, which is the strongest available signal of operational maturity [sportway-01]. Cameras are wired to mains and to on site or datacentre computers, with no batteries or phone hotspots involved [sportway-16]. Public reliability complaints are not visible because the service is sold to federations and consumers review the TV 2 Play app, so the camera itself gets no public reviews.
criteria.portability_install: Installation is a one time fixed mount per rink or pitch, with the club providing power and internet and Sportway supplying and installing all equipment at its own cost [sportway-06, sportway-12]. Nothing is portable, so away fixtures at unequipped venues are not captured. The Studio App lets a person produce a match manually from a smartphone where no fixed camera exists [sportway-14].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Cameras connect by cable to a local or datacentre computer and the club supplies a fast internet line, with hockey.nl stating a fast connection is one of the two things a club must provide [sportway-16, sportway-12]. Bandwidth requirements are not published.
criteria.workflow_ux: Matches are scheduled automatically from federation databases, so clubs do not start or stop recordings [sportway-14]. Coaches tag events in the Team Account and players clip and share from the Player Account, both web based [sportway-14]. Viewers use the federation web TV or the MyGame app inside TV 2 Play [sportway-04].
criteria.analysis_layer: Team Account offers real time tagging of shots, goals, turnovers and face offs plus video markup for player feedback [sportway-14]. Player Account gives a personal highlights library, statistics and recruitment reel creation [sportway-14]. This is a broadcast first product and it lacks the tactical drawing tools and fitness data of dedicated analysis platforms.
criteria.integrations: Auto scheduling integrates with federation and league match databases [sportway-14]. In Norway the player opt out runs through the national Min Idrett registration system, which shows deep federation IT integration [sportway-06]. Public APIs for third party analysis tools are not documented.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is the core product, through Playsite white label OTT with pay per view and subscription billing, browser and mobile apps and TV casting [sportway-14]. Recent examples include ClubhockeyTV inside Hockey.nl, Volleybal TV for Nevobo, WKBLive.tv for English ice hockey clubs and the Prva CFL platform in Montenegro [sportway-11, sportway-18]. In Norway, distribution is through TV 2 Play at NOK 139 a month [sportway-05].
criteria.data_access_ownership: Sportway's model is that the operator holds the rights and the platform, and MyGame states that videos are removed after two to three months depending on the tournament [sportway-06]. Player Account allows clip editing and social sharing, and full match download rights for clubs are not documented publicly [sportway-14]. Clubs entering a deal should negotiate raw footage access and retention in the contract.
criteria.privacy_compliance: MyGame streams only from the 15 year age class, requires athletes to be at least 13, lets any player opt out anonymously through Min Idrett, blocks filming of players with protected addresses by default and shares data controller duties with the Norwegian sports confederation after working with the Data Protection Authority [sportway-06]. That framework was built after municipalities in Oslo, Bergen, Trondheim and Tromsø paused cameras in 2023 and after training sessions were filmed without notice in 2022 [sportway-08, sportway-09, sportway-10]. For ClubhockeyTV the KNHB requires advance information to players, coaches and officials and gives clubs consent guidelines, and no automatic blurring feature is described anywhere [sportway-11, sportway-12].
criteria.security: Not assessable from public sources. MyGame refers to a two level security solution for personal data without technical detail [sportway-06].
criteria.pricing_tco: Clubs inside a federation agreement pay nothing for hardware, installation or operation, and supply only power and internet [sportway-06, sportway-12]. Consumers in Norway pay NOK 139 a month or NOK 1,199 a year, with 20% of subscription revenue paid to the club the subscriber selects, and MyGame reports NOK 7.9 million paid out to Norwegian sport [sportway-05, sportway-04]. Federation platform fees, revenue splits outside Norway and any per club option are not public, so total cost for a federation is a negotiated number.
criteria.support_service: Sportway runs country teams, with a named Italy project manager and a Sportway NL entity with its own CEO for the Dutch rollout [sportway-02, sportway-11]. The Swedish switchboard and info address are the public contact points [sportway-03]. Service levels for clubs are not published.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Sportway raised EUR 20 million in June 2026 at a EUR 92 million post money valuation, led by Gamma Waves with existing shareholders participating, to fund international expansion, product development and acquisitions [sportway-01]. It bought Studio Automated with Broadcast Solutions in April 2026 and signed EuroHockey, Spanish basketball, Swedish futsal and Swedish handball deals between June and September 2026 [sportway-15, sportway-18]. The holding company showed a SEK 14.2 million loss for 2024 with 14 employees at holding level, so the group is still investing ahead of profit [sportway-17].
criteria.evidence_references: Reference customers named in primary material include the Swedish and Finnish ice hockey associations, KNHB, Nevobo, the Norwegian tennis and padel federation, FISG in Italy and the Norwegian sports confederation through MyGame [sportway-01, sportway-02, sportway-06, sportway-18]. Published football references are limited to Montenegro's Prva CFL OTT platform and 2,000 matches a season without named clubs [sportway-03, sportway-18].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Not assessable from public sources. Norwegian coverage records club leaders defending the service when municipalities switched cameras off, which is a satisfaction signal from administrators, and analysts have left no public record [sportway-08].
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Cameras feed a computer on site or in a datacentre where the AI framing runs, and MyGame describes this as cable connected processing with no compute in the camera [sportway-16]. Studio Automated brings server side real time event detection [sportway-15]. Data residency for stored video is not published.
criteria.accessibility_languages: The corporate site is in English and country pages exist for Italy and Norway, while MyGame is in Norwegian and ClubhockeyTV is delivered in Dutch inside Hockey.nl [sportway-02, sportway-04, sportway-12]. App language lists and accessibility features are not published.
criteria.upgrade_path: Within a deal, clubs can move from automated fixed capture to Studio App manual production and up to AI PTZ multicamera production from Studio Automated [sportway-14, sportway-15]. Coaching layers, low latency betting feeds and the Situation Room safety review tool are add ons on the same platform [sportway-14].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the opt out flow end to end, since the anonymous Min Idrett reservation is the most mature consent mechanism in this market and it should be a contract requirement anywhere minors are filmed [sportway-06]. Test the real time highlight and replay generation now that Studio Automated is in house [sportway-15]. Ask for the club revenue share formula and compare it with MyGame's published 20% [sportway-06].

free.name: Staige (Staige One AG, formerly soccerwatch.tv)
free.payer_model_label: Platform pays for cameras and shares revenue
free.one_line: A fixed 180-degree AI camera bolted to a floodlight pole that streams amateur matches to the Staige TV platform, sells virtual tickets and sponsor banners on the club's behalf, and feeds a coaching app.
free.who_for: German-speaking amateur and semi-professional clubs that want every home match streamed without a volunteer behind a camera, and that have a sponsor or a regional bank willing to fund the hardware. Federations and broadcasters that want a turnkey lower-league feed are the second audience.
free.why: Staige exists because soccerwatch.tv proved in 2017 that German amateur clubs would let a robot camera film them if the stream came with sponsor money attached, and the K2 panorama camera plus the Staige TV paywall turned that into a repeatable product with more than 250,000 events recorded [staige-06]. It matters now because the listed parent Staige One AG has spent 2025 and 2026 moving its capital and its engineers into Staige for Industries, a security and infrastructure video business, while the sport segment sits flat at about €2.0 million revenue and camera deliveries run behind schedule [staige-05, staige-07]. It tells you that the pure sponsor-funded amateur streaming model, on its own, has struggled to carry a listed company, and that the survivors in this space will be the ones with a second revenue engine or a very lean cost base.
free.price_band: Camera pricing on request, typically sponsor or bank funded; €1.50 net per paid pay-per-view access retained by Staige

italy.note: The 2025 annual report lists Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, the USA and China as markets and does not mention Italy, and an earlier regional profile named Italy only as an expansion target [staige-05, staige-10].

verdict.look_if: You run a club in Germany, Austria, Switzerland or Luxembourg with a permanent floodlit main pitch, a fixed 230V supply at height and a sponsor or regional bank prepared to cover the camera, and your main aim is an unattended weekly stream plus a paywall, with tracking data a low priority. Look also if you are a small federation or regional broadcaster that wants dozens of venues streamed under one platform contract with sponsor and pay-per-view tooling already built.
verdict.skip_if: You are outside the DACH region, you want a portable device you can carry to away games, or you need positional and event data on top of video, because Staige Coach is a video tagging tool and the K2X is a fixed install. Skip also if you need the vendor to be around and investing in sport for the next five years without question, because the parent company's own auditor has flagged going concern uncertainty and management is directing capital to the industrial video business.
watch_outs: The 2025 consolidated accounts carry an auditor's note of material uncertainty about the group's ability to continue as a going concern, with financing dependent on shareholder loans from adesso SE and Malo Industriebeteiligungen [staige-05].
Sport segment revenue was flat at €2.04 million in 2025 and management says deliveries of the new camera generation to licence customers are running behind schedule [staige-05, staige-08].
Camera purchase and subscription prices are not published, so every deal is negotiated through a consultation call and a sponsor or funding partner [staige-02, staige-03].

The StaigeTV viewer app on iOS carries a 2.6 out of 5 rating from 69 reviews, with complaints about streams failing to start and cropped horizontal playback, and its last update listed is December 2024 [staige-12].
Staige retains €1.50 net on every paid pay-per-view access and settles paywall credits to the club only once or twice a year [staige-01].
Full match downloads require a separate desktop download tool for Mac or Windows, with no one-click export in the web app [staige-01].
Headcount fell from 49.5 average employees in H1 2025 to 37 in H1 2026, and the year-end 2025 count was 29 FTE, so support capacity for sport customers is thinner than it was [staige-05, staige-07].

criteria.use_case_fit: Staige is built for the fixed home ground of an amateur or semi-professional club, with the camera mounted at about seven metres on a floodlight pole and a permanent 230V feed, and it covers football first with volleyball, handball, basketball, ice hockey and equestrian as secondary sports [staige-01, staige-02]. The product answers the streaming and monetisation question well and the coaching question adequately. It does not answer the away-match question at all, since even the K2X, marketed as portable and ready in five minutes, is sold to clubs as a floodlight-pole install in the club material [staige-02, staige-03].
criteria.capture_quality: The K2 records and streams in Full HD from six lenses stitched into a 180-degree panorama, and the annual report describes a new camera generation with resolution moved from 8K to 16K source capture for the ClipMyHorse.TV equestrian deployment [staige-01, staige-05, staige-14]. Output to viewers remains HD, and each 130-minute game consumes 8 to 12 GB upstream [staige-01]. Public sample footage on Staige TV shows a competent broadcast-style virtual camera at amateur grounds, with the usual panorama softness at the far touchline.
criteria.automation_accuracy: The system tracks players and ball in real time and produces an AI-directed virtual camera, with alternative streams for training, analysis and full 180-degree views selectable per event [staige-01]. Staige publishes no accuracy figures and no independent test exists in public, so the evidence is limited to the platform's operating history of more than 250,000 recorded events and the RTL Luxembourg and CA Osasuna academy references [staige-03, staige-06]. Highlight generation is automatic with a tagging tool for manual correction [staige-01].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Stitching happens inside the single camera head across six sensors, so there is no field calibration for the club to do and no second unit to align [staige-01]. Multiple output perspectives are all cut from the same single panorama. There is no public support for combining two K2 units or an external PTZ into one production.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live streaming is the core use case, with simultaneous output to Staige TV, YouTube and Twitch, pre-roll advertising and up to six sponsor banners inserted in the stream [staige-01, staige-03]. Staige publishes no glass-to-glass latency figure. The company learned the hard way about scale after a server failure during an FC Schalke 04 test match with more than 40,000 viewers, which it says drove infrastructure changes [staige-10].
criteria.reliability_resilience: The camera is weatherproof and tamper resistant, draws 29W while streaming and 10W in standby, and runs unattended on a schedule [staige-01, staige-14]. The main public signal on reliability is the viewer app, where iOS reviewers report streams that fail to start and slow loading, summarised by one reviewer as a world-class idea with lower-league execution [staige-12]. Vendor headcount cuts through 2025 and 2026 are a second risk to operational responsiveness [staige-05, staige-07].
criteria.portability_install: Installation of the K2 takes one to two hours on a floodlight pole at roughly seven metres and requires permanent mains power and a wired or strong wireless uplink [staige-01, staige-03]. The K2X page promises a five-minute mobile setup, yet the same site sells it to clubs as a pole-mounted install, and no battery, tripod or LTE specification is published for the mobile use case [staige-02]. Treat Staige as a fixed system until the vendor shows you a portable kit in the field.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Staige requires 8 to 12 Mbps sustained upload per camera and produces 8 to 12 GB of data per game, which rules out many rural club grounds without a dedicated line [staige-01]. All processing and storage is cloud based in Frankfurt and the Netherlands, so there is no server hardware at the club [staige-01]. No offline recording fallback is described in public material.
criteria.workflow_ux: Clubs manage schedules, banners and paywall settings in the Backstaige dashboard, viewers use Staige TV on web and mobile, and coaches use Staige Coach for drawing, tagging and sharing clips to players' phones [staige-01, staige-03]. Full-match download needs a separate desktop tool [staige-01]. The viewer app's 2.6 rating suggests the fan-facing side lags the club-facing side [staige-12].
criteria.analysis_layer: Staige Coach offers video review with drawing tools, tagging and clip sharing, endorsed in vendor material by Borussia Dortmund and the CA Osasuna academy [staige-03]. There is no positional tracking data, no event data feed and no xG-style metrics offered to clubs in public material. For a club that wants data, this is a stream first and a coaching tool second.
criteria.integrations: Streams push to YouTube and Twitch alongside Staige TV, and broadcasters such as RTL Luxembourg, FAN.at and ClipMyHorse.TV take Staige feeds into their own services [staige-01]. There is no published API, no XML export for Hudl or Sportscode, and no listed integration with club management or ticketing software. Integration therefore means distribution endpoints, with no data exchange.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is Staige's strongest layer, with a hosted OTT platform, pay-per-view and season tickets, sponsor banner management for up to six partners, pre-roll ads and social highlight clips with sponsor logos [staige-01, staige-03]. Staige keeps €1.50 net per paid access for processing and payment provider costs and credits the club once or twice a year [staige-01]. The club keeps its sponsorship revenue in full under the Volksbank funding programme description [staige-13].
criteria.data_access_ownership: Clubs can download complete games through the desktop tool and share clips from Staige Coach, and recordings are stored on European servers [staige-01]. The published material does not state who owns the footage, how long it is retained, or whether Staige may reuse it for model training, and the company's 2025 report describes data from more than 250,000 events as a company asset [staige-06]. Ask for the licence terms in writing before signing.
criteria.privacy_compliance: Staige publishes a sample privacy notice for facilities, lights a red signal lamp during recording, permanently blurs areas such as residential buildings or footpaths on request, and stores data in Frankfurt and the Netherlands [staige-01]. The parent company positions its industrial product around privacy by design, no facial recognition and EU AI Act alignment, which the sport product inherits at platform level [staige-07]. There is no published consent workflow for minors on the pitch, which matters for youth football.
criteria.security: The company is majority owned by adesso SE and describes enterprise-grade scalability and certified IT security standards through that relationship, with hosting in the EU [staige-04, staige-01]. No ISO 27001 certificate, penetration test summary or SOC report for the sport platform is public. Not assessable beyond these statements from public sources.
criteria.pricing_tco: No purchase, lease or subscription price for the K2 or K2X is published; clubs are routed to a consultation and to sponsor or bank funding, with the Volksbank eG Gestalterbank programme giving four clubs a year a free system with storage for about 120 games annually [staige-02, staige-13]. The annual report describes sale-and-leaseback financing of cameras on about 32-month terms, which points to a multi-year commitment [staige-05]. Known recurring costs are the €1.50 net per paid access and the club's own upload line [staige-01].
criteria.support_service: Club support runs through a dedicated email and a German phone line in Essen, with installation done by Staige or partners in one to two hours [staige-02, staige-03]. Headcount has fallen to 29 FTE at year-end 2025 and 37 on average in H1 2026, with a restructured sales organisation, so response capacity is thinner than it was [staige-05, staige-07]. No public SLA is published.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Staige One AG is listed in Frankfurt and Düsseldorf, reported €2.0 million revenue and a €4.2 million net loss for 2025, raised €2.1 million in a Q2 2025 capital increase mostly taken up by adesso SE and Malo Industriebeteiligungen, and took a further €0.6 million credit line in March 2026 and about €0.85 million more in shareholder loans by August 2026 [staige-06, staige-08]. H1 2026 revenue was €1.03 million with EBITDA of minus €0.47 million, improved from minus €1.51 million, and management targets €3.0 to 3.5 million revenue and break-even EBITDA for the full year, driven by Staige for Industries with sport flat [staige-07]. The auditor's going concern note and the flat sport line are the two facts to weigh [staige-05].
criteria.evidence_references: Named references include Borussia Dortmund as shareholder and user, the CA Osasuna academy, RTL Luxembourg, FAN.at and ClipMyHorse.TV, plus more than 200 club partnerships and 1,200 games streamed weekly in an earlier regional profile [staige-03, staige-10]. The homepage claims more than 1,200 installed systems across all business lines [staige-04]. No independent field test or federation evaluation is public.
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Vendor testimonials from BVB's Lars Ricken and the Osasuna academy's Imanol Lobo praise real-time analysis and direct sharing with players [staige-03]. Independent coach reviews are absent, and the public sentiment that exists concerns the fan app, where playback problems dominate [staige-12]. Not assessable for the coaching tool from independent public sources.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: The camera stitches and encodes on the device, then everything else runs in the cloud, including the AI direction, highlights, storage and delivery [staige-01]. There is no local recording option described for grounds without an uplink. The industrial product line is edge based, and the annual report references a newer camera generation, so more on-device processing may arrive in sport, though no date is given [staige-05, staige-07].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The website, apps and support operate in German and English, and the viewer app is listed in English only on the App Store [staige-01, staige-12]. Broadcasters in Luxembourg and Austria use the platform, which shows multi-market operation inside the German-speaking area [staige-01]. No Italian, Spanish or French interface is documented.
criteria.upgrade_path: Existing licence customers are being moved to the new camera generation during 2026, with deliveries behind plan [staige-08]. A club can grow from a single K2 to Staige Pro deployments for leagues and broadcasters under the same platform [staige-04]. There is no published trade-in or firmware roadmap for clubs.
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the paywall and sponsor banner workflow end to end, including how quickly a virtual ticket purchase resolves to a playing stream on a phone, since that is where Staige claims to earn the club money [staige-01]. Test the Staige Coach clip-to-player flow with a youth squad and check the consent handling. Ask for the current delivery date of the new camera generation and the contract term behind any sponsor-funded offer [staige-05, staige-08].

free.payer_model_label: Club pays for a coaching tool
free.one_line: A Korean-founded analysis company that sells a fixed or portable dual-lens 4K panoramic camera bundled with a cloud analysis suite, human-verified event data and optional video-based tracking data, aimed at academies and semi-professional clubs.
free.who_for: Academies, semi-professional first teams and federations that already employ an analyst and want FIFA-qualified panoramic footage plus tagged event data delivered back within a day, with the option to add tracking-derived physical metrics without GPS vests. Fan streaming is a side benefit.
free.why: BEPRO exists because a Seoul team of analysts worked out in 2015 that the expensive part of football data was the human tagging, and that if you controlled the camera you could industrialise the tagging and sell it to clubs the big data houses ignored [bepro-12, bepro-20]. It matters now because the 2025 Cerberus OS3 release with RTMP live coding into Sportscode, the Camera Station that accepts any IP camera, and published dollar pricing for the portable kit mark a shift from bespoke fixed installs toward a self-serve product for smaller clubs [bepro-10, bepro-09, bepro-02]. It tells you that the analysis-first vendors are moving down market into the same academies that Veo and Pixellot serve from the streaming side, and that data delivered with the video, ahead of the camera itself, is where they intend to win.
free.price_band: USD 2,000 one-off for the Cerberus portable camera plus USD 1,000 per year (or USD 83.33 per month) for BEPRO Space and Editor software, VAT excluded; fixed camera and event data services on quotation

italy.note: BEPRO lists Italy among its office countries, has been the video analysis partner of the Divisione Calcio a 5 for Serie A futsal with a renewal announced in October 2024, and installed fixed cameras at Bologna FC's youth training grounds in December 2020 under an Italian business director [bepro-08, bepro-15, bepro-16].

free.evidence_note: Portable camera, software, quadpod and platform prices are read directly from the vendor's pages in USD; fixed camera and data service prices are on quotation; corporate financials for the Korean parent are not public and the Hamburg entity's latest filed accounts are for 2021.

verdict.look_if: You have an analyst or a coach who will use event data and clips every week, you want the tagging done for you, and you are comfortable with a USD-priced contract from a company headquartered in Seoul with a Hamburg legal entity for European terms. Look also if you need to feed live panoramic video into Sportscode or Nacsport on the bench, which the Cerberus does over RTMP.
verdict.skip_if: Your priority is a fan-facing live stream with sponsor overlays and a paywall, because BEPRO offers no OTT layer of its own and its live path is aimed at analysts. Skip also if you need transparent published pricing for the fixed system or the data services, or if you want the recording available within minutes of the final whistle, since the portable camera uploads 30 to 60 minutes after the match on the vendor's own figures.
watch_outs: The terms of use grant BEPRO a non-exclusive, unlimited, gratuitous, non-revocable, transferable and worldwide right to use submitted content for commercial and non-commercial purposes, which covers your match footage [bepro-11].
Prices on the site are shown in USD with VAT excluded and no currency selector, so a European club should confirm the EUR invoice amount and the entity that bills it [bepro-02, bepro-04].

The software bundle sold with the camera is USD 1,000 per year, while the standalone BEPRO Space and Editor page lists USD 5,000 per year or USD 500 per month, and the site does not explain which tier a club receives [bepro-02, bepro-04].
Upload of a two-hour match completes within one hour in about 72% of the 184 recordings BEPRO cites, which means roughly one match in four takes longer [bepro-02].
The Hamburg entity Bepro Europe GmbH has €25,000 share capital, sits at a WeWork address and its most recent filed accounts are for 2021, so European counterparty substance is thin [bepro-17].
No Korean parent financials, headcount or post-2020 funding rounds are public, and the last disclosed raise was €8.8 million in June 2020 [bepro-12, bepro-18].
Resolution, weight, lens and storage specifications for the Cerberus are absent from the product page, which describes battery life and upload behaviour only [bepro-02].

criteria.use_case_fit: BEPRO is an analysis product first, with FIFA-qualified 4K panoramic recording feeding event tagging, interactive reports, positional data and a collaborative editor, and its named users run from Larne FC and the Accrington Stanley academy to the Spain national team at Euro 2024 and the K League technical study group [bepro-01, bepro-20, bepro-14]. Academies with a staff analyst are the sweet spot. A grassroots club with no analyst will pay for data it will struggle to use.
criteria.capture_quality: The company describes FIFA-qualified 4K panoramic capture from two internal cameras stitched into one wide feed, with the OS3 update adding steadier zoom scale and better framing from off-centre positions [bepro-01, bepro-10]. The soccerscene profile notes the system scored well above industry standard in most FIFA certification assessments with no score below above industry standard [bepro-20]. The Cerberus page publishes no sensor, lens, frame rate or bitrate figures, so quality claims rest on the FIFA qualification and sample footage [bepro-02].
criteria.automation_accuracy: Recording is fully automatic with no operator, and the AI View was upgraded in June 2025 to reduce excessive zooming, track the ball more precisely and crop out areas beyond the pitch [bepro-10]. Event data is collected to FIFA definitions with every data point linked to video for verification, and advanced data adds xG, xT, line-breaking passes and packing from video tracking without GPS [bepro-21, bepro-06]. BEPRO publishes no accuracy percentages for the automatic framing, and the human tagging layer is what carries data accuracy.
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: The Cerberus stitches its two internal cameras on the device, and the BEPRO Camera Station released in July 2025 ingests any IP camera into the same system for fixed installs, which lets a club combine BEPRO and third-party cameras under one recording pipeline [bepro-10, bepro-09, bepro-05]. Multi-angle production for broadcast is not offered. The panoramic feed plus a tactical view and a proprietary 3D player are the viewing modes [bepro-01].
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Cerberus OS3 added RTMP output so analysts can live code in Sportscode, SBG or Nacsport from a laptop connected to the camera, and the Editor supports live coding over a stadium network or a direct cable [bepro-10, bepro-07]. Real-time review on the pitch, including at half-time, is a stated feature of the fixed system [bepro-05]. There is no fan streaming product, no published latency figure and no built-in RTMP push to YouTube described on the product pages.
criteria.reliability_resilience: The camera is weather resistant for rain and snow, runs 4.5 hours or more per swappable battery with 9 hours or more on a spare, and OS3 fixed quality degradation from heat during long recordings [bepro-02, bepro-10]. Upload completed within an hour for about 72% of 184 two-hour recordings in the vendor's own data, which is honest and also means a quarter of matches arrive later [bepro-02]. Independent reliability reports are absent; the App Store rating of 4.7 rests on 10 reviews [bepro-19].
criteria.portability_install: The portable kit is the Cerberus on the 7.6-metre four-legged BEPRO Quadpod, which weighs 6.5 kg against 12 kg for a conventional 7.7-metre tripod and ships in a wheeled carrier that doubles as a backpack, with stabilisers included [bepro-03]. The fixed camera is permanently installed and scheduled for the season, with the Camera Station making install a matter of power and network [bepro-05]. Setup time for the portable kit is not stated.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: The camera creates its own WiFi network for control from the mobile app or Editor, processes video during recording and uploads afterwards, with 30 to 60 minutes typical for a two-hour match [bepro-02]. No LTE modem, no Ethernet port and no minimum upload speed are listed for the portable camera. The fixed system needs power and network at the venue [bepro-05].
criteria.workflow_ux: BEPRO Space runs on web, mobile and tablet with schedule filters, full match and clip video, team and player data, a shared library with recovery of deleted items, and an in-app messenger for sending clips to players, while BEPRO Editor adds Google Docs style simultaneous editing, presentation files, secondary tags with pivot tables and XML import from Sportscode [bepro-04, bepro-07, bepro-09]. The mobile app was fully redesigned in September 2025 [bepro-09]. This is an analyst's toolset with a lot of surface area, a long way from a two-button club app.
criteria.analysis_layer: Three data tiers exist: standard event data to FIFA definitions with heatmaps and interactive reports, advanced data using video tracking for xG, xT, xA, packing, runs in behind and physical metrics for both teams without GPS, and bespoke reports, plus a Data API and raw tracking files for clubs that want to process data themselves [bepro-21, bepro-06, bepro-01]. Analysis covers football, futsal, basketball and handball [bepro-21]. The article by the vendor's Australian profile puts output at about three million data points per 90 minutes [bepro-20].
criteria.integrations: RTMP into Sportscode, SBG and Nacsport, XML import from Sportscode into the Editor, IP camera ingest through the Camera Station and a Data API cover the main integration paths [bepro-10, bepro-07, bepro-09, bepro-01]. There is no listed integration with club management, ticketing or OTT platforms. Video export from the Editor allows clips and custom views to be downloaded or shared [bepro-07].
criteria.distribution_ott: BEPRO has no fan-facing platform, paywall or sponsor overlay product; distribution is internal to the club through BEPRO Space and the messenger [bepro-04]. A club wanting to stream to supporters would need to take the RTMP feed into its own encoder or platform, which the product pages do not describe [bepro-10]. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Users retain ownership of uploaded content and can download team and player data, clips, custom views and raw tracking files [bepro-11, bepro-04, bepro-06]. The same terms give BEPRO a non-exclusive, unlimited, non-revocable, transferable worldwide licence to use submitted content commercially, and retention periods and hosting location are not specified beyond a centralised cloud [bepro-11]. Clubs with sensitive academy footage should negotiate this clause.
criteria.privacy_compliance: German law and Hamburg jurisdiction apply to commercial clients through Bepro Europe GmbH, and the terms note that user activity may be monitored within legal limits with IP data collected [bepro-11]. No consent workflow for filmed minors, no blurring feature and no data processing agreement template are published. Not assessable beyond the terms from public sources.
criteria.security: Data is stored in a centralised cloud with no stated region, and no certification, penetration test or access control documentation is public [bepro-11]. Not assessable from public sources.
criteria.pricing_tco: The Cerberus portable camera is USD 2,000 one-off with BEPRO Space and Editor at USD 83.33 per month or USD 1,000 per year, the Quadpod is USD 500, and the standalone Space plus Editor subscription is USD 500 per month or USD 5,000 per year (USD 416.67 per month), all VAT excluded [bepro-02, bepro-03, bepro-04]. Fixed cameras, the Camera Station, standard and advanced data and bespoke reports are all on quotation [bepro-05, bepro-21, bepro-06]. A first-year portable setup is therefore about USD 3,500 before tax and before any data service, with the data service the real cost driver for most clubs.
criteria.support_service: The site offers demos, a free trial and contact sales routes, and the company says it has offices in the UK, USA, Germany, Spain, Italy, South Korea, Japan and Vietnam with a London address published [bepro-08, bepro-01]. No SLA, support hours or response commitments are public. Not assessable beyond this from public sources.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: BEPRO raised €7.9 million in 2018 and €8.8 million in June 2020 from Altos Ventures, SoftBank Ventures, Saehan Ventures, Springcamp and Mirae Asset Ventures, and no later round is public [bepro-12]. The Korean parent Bepro Company Co., Ltd. discloses no revenue or headcount on Korean business portals, and the Hamburg entity's last filed accounts cover 2021 [bepro-18, bepro-17]. Product cadence in 2025 and 2026 is steady, with six shipped updates listed from June 2025 to May 2026, which is the best public health signal available [bepro-09].
criteria.evidence_references: Named references include the Spain national team at Euro 2024, the K League technical study group, the KFA Golden Pass youth programme, Regionalliga Nordost, the Divisione Calcio a 5, Bologna FC's youth sector, Larne FC and the Accrington Stanley academy, and the vendor claims more than 2,400 teams across 50 nations and more than 500,000 matches analysed [bepro-20, bepro-14, bepro-13, bepro-15, bepro-16, bepro-01]. FIFA qualification of the camera is the one third-party technical validation [bepro-01, bepro-20].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Public sentiment is thin: the BEPRO Sports app holds 4.7 from 10 ratings with praise for real-time stats and a request for more frequent updates, and the Korean employer review site rates the company 3.1 out of 5 [bepro-19, bepro-18]. Federation quotes from the KFA and K League are positive about data quality and scientific youth development [bepro-13, bepro-14]. No independent club review of the Cerberus is public.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: The Cerberus processes video on the device during recording so that upload can start as soon as the match ends, and it exposes RTMP locally for live coding without cloud dependency [bepro-02, bepro-10]. Event tagging and advanced tracking happen in BEPRO's cloud and analyst operation, with a turnaround the site does not quantify. The fixed Camera Station is a plug-and-play on-site processing unit [bepro-05].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The mobile app supports English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean and Spanish, and the website runs in English with a Korean version [bepro-19, bepro-01]. Office presence in Italy and Spain suggests local-language sales support, though no Italian support line is published [bepro-08].
criteria.upgrade_path: A club can start with the portable Cerberus and software, add standard then advanced data, move to a fixed install through the Camera Station with any IP camera, and take raw tracking or the Data API when it has its own data staff [bepro-02, bepro-05, bepro-06]. Camera firmware updates ship over the air, as OS3 did in June 2025 [bepro-10]. No trade-in terms are published.
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the RTMP live coding path into your existing Sportscode or Nacsport licence on the bench, since that is BEPRO's clearest technical edge among portable cameras [bepro-10]. Time the upload on your own connection across three matches and compare against the 72% within-one-hour figure [bepro-02]. Order one match of advanced data and check the tracking-derived physical numbers against a GPS session before committing to a season [bepro-06].

free.one_line: Hudl Focus is the camera family of the Hudl analysis platform, with fixed Indoor and Outdoor units, a static Focus Point and the portable Focus Flex, all of which upload automatically into a Hudl subscription that is required to use them [hf-01, hf-07].
free.who_for: Clubs and academies that already live inside Hudl, Sportscode or Wyscout and want the film to arrive without an operator, with the Flex packaged for semi-professional and amateur football from 2,000 dollars including a Bronze subscription [hf-03, hf-11]. US schools that want a permanent stadium or gym camera with livestreaming to Hudl TV, since broadcasting is limited to the fixed units [hf-01, hf-07].
free.why: Hudl Focus exists because Hudl owned the coaching workflow and needed to own the capture point too, so the camera is sold as a way to feed the subscription, and it has never been priced as a product in its own right [hf-07, hf-05]. It matters now because the Flex, refreshed in February 2024 with a three-hour battery and automatic calibration, is the only portable camera bundled with Assist stat breakdowns and Wyscout tagging, which makes Hudl the incumbent choice for any club that already pays for those tools [hf-09, hf-12, hf-03]. It tells you the space is consolidating around platforms, with Hudl adding Balltime, Titan and TeamUp in 2025 and 2026 while publishing no camera price and no Focus product news at all [hf-17, hf-18].
free.price_band: Focus cameras carry no list price and are sold inside quoted club or athletic-department packages; the one published camera bundle is the mid-market soccer Team Pack from USD 2,000 with a Flex; soccer software runs USD 500 to 2,500 per team per year (Core, Plus, Premier), US high school programs USD 1,500 to 4,000 per program per year, and every sport and segment has its own price grid [hf-03, hf-23, hf-24, hf-25]

criteria.use_case_fit: Focus Indoor and Outdoor are permanent auto-tracking cameras for gyms and stadiums, Focus Point is a static panoramic angle for end zones and endlines, and Focus Flex is the portable unit marketed to football and hockey clubs [hf-01, hf-02]. Tracking algorithms cover American football, football, lacrosse, basketball, volleyball and wrestling on the fixed units, while the Flex is marketed for the football pitch and hockey rink [hf-07, hf-06]. The semi-professional and amateur football offer packages the Flex with Bronze, Silver or Gold storage and Assist services [hf-03, hf-04].
criteria.capture_quality: Hudl describes Focus output as HD or 1080p and publishes no sensor or frame rate figures for any model [hf-02, hf-05]. Focus Indoor records a 180 degree panorama with real-time ball tracking and stereo audio in a 3.18 kilogram unit, and the Flex carries 500 gigabytes of storage for more than 100 matches, a three-hour battery with an external battery option, and an extra-wide tactical angle framing 20 or more players [hf-08, hf-06, hf-09]. Night mode exposure was improved in the 2024 Flex update [hf-09].
criteria.automation_accuracy: The 2024 Flex update improved the ball tracking algorithm, increased default zoom for tactical review and added multi-angle capture in practice mode [hf-09]. Hudl publishes no tracking accuracy figures, and the fixed FAQ notes that tracking algorithms exist only for the listed sports [hf-07]. Bromley FC's head of academy analysis describes sessions uploaded and ready to analyse by the time notes are finished [hf-11].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Focus Point supplies a second static angle that Hudl positions as a supplementary view to a primary camera [hf-01]. Flex practice mode captures multiple angles from one unit, and Sportscode integration supports live coding workflows [hf-09, hf-01]. There is no cloud production switcher and no third-party camera ingest in the Focus product [hf-01].
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Fixed Focus cameras stream to Hudl TV with pay-per-view control, to YouTube free of charge, or to any RTMP-capable broadcast software [hf-07, hf-01]. Focus Flex and Focus Point cannot broadcast on the product page, although the Flex FAQ and soccer page describe livestreaming to Hudl TV over 4G or Wi-Fi with 4G limited to the US, so confirm current capability in writing [hf-01, hf-06, hf-11]. Hudl publishes no latency figures [hf-07].
criteria.reliability_resilience: Fixed cameras record offline against the schedule and upload when the connection returns [hf-08]. The Hudl Focus app scores 4.0 from 40 iOS ratings and 4.2 from 44 Google Play reviews, with one coach reporting only two of seven games recorded in a season because of connectivity problems [hf-15, hf-16]. Hudl says it reviews failures outside warranty and provides hardware replacements at no cost, without stating the warranty length [hf-07].
criteria.portability_install: Fixed units install in 60 to 90 minutes by the customer or a contractor with a drill, ladder or lift and a Cat5e or Cat6 run, and Hudl charges nothing for installation [hf-07]. The Flex ships with tripod, stabilisation kit and app control and calibrates automatically without a direct phone connection since 2024 [hf-11, hf-09]. The Indoor unit measures 12.7 by 25.4 by 20.3 centimetres and weighs 3.18 kilograms [hf-08].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Fixed cameras need a hardwired Ethernet connection and do not support Wi-Fi, and Hudl publishes no minimum upload speed on its FAQ [hf-07]. The Flex uploads in real time over Wi-Fi or a Hudl 4G data plan sold separately and available in the US only [hf-02, hf-06]. Video is described as available on Hudl before the gear comes off with no processing wait [hf-02].
criteria.workflow_ux: Film lands in the Hudl library with 1080p playback, mobile apps, team messaging and email support on all club tiers, with game-time phone support on Gold [hf-05]. Assist delivers analyst-produced stat breakdowns and Wyscout Tag on Demand returns tagged matches within 48 hours [hf-03, hf-12]. App reviewers ask for tighter Sideline integration and complain about repetitive setup screens on every launch [hf-15, hf-16].
criteria.analysis_layer: Hudl Assist Unlimited Game and Unlimited Scout are bundled in the Coach and Analyst packs, giving team and opponent statistics linked to video [hf-03]. Titan GPS wearables, acquired in June 2025, and Balltime volleyball AI, acquired in February 2025, sit alongside as add-ons [hf-18, hf-05]. Sportscode and Wyscout provide the professional analysis and scouting layers under the same owner [hf-01, hf-20].
criteria.integrations: Focus integrates natively with Hudl, Hudl Sportscode for live coding, Hudl TV and, through Wyscout Tag on Demand, with the scouting platform [hf-01, hf-12]. Fixed cameras output an RTMP feed usable by third-party broadcast software [hf-07]. Reviewers request RTMP on the app for the Flex, which suggests it is absent there [hf-15].
criteria.distribution_ott: Hudl TV carries streams from fixed Focus cameras with pay-per-view and monetisation controls, and YouTube streaming is free [hf-01, hf-07]. Hudl signed a five-year streaming deal with the Great Lakes Valley Conference in September 2025 and ticketing and streaming deals with US school associations [hf-17]. Portable units do not broadcast per the product page [hf-01].
criteria.data_access_ownership: Storage is metered per team and per sport, at 50, 100 and 200 hours on the soccer Core, Plus and Premier tiers and 30, 100 and 200 hours on the American football Bronze, Silver and Gold tiers, and film beyond the cap depends on the plan [hf-23, hf-05, hf-03]. Hudl treats athlete video as user-generated content and retains data for as long as necessary without stated periods [hf-13]. Export rights for full-match files are not described on the Focus pages, so confirm them in the agreement [hf-01].
criteria.privacy_compliance: Hudl's privacy policy, updated 11 August 2026, positions Hudl as controller, transfers EU and UK data under standard contractual clauses, stores data in various locations and requires verified parental consent for users under 13, with a data protection officer reachable at dpo@hudl.com [hf-13]. AI player matching uses jersey numbers, clothing and general appearance with manual coach verification, and no face blurring or on-pitch opt-out is described [hf-13]. Rights of non-users appearing in footage are not addressed [hf-13].
criteria.security: Hudl offers a SOC 2 report, penetration test attestation letters, HECVAT, TXRAMP and PCI documents on request, aligns its programme with NIST 800-53, encrypts data in transit and at rest, replicates across availability zones with daily and weekly backups and commits to breach notification typically within 72 hours [hf-14]. A public status page runs at status.hudl.com [hf-14]. Hosting provider and regions are not disclosed [hf-14].
criteria.pricing_tco: Hudl prices by a grid, and the grid is the first thing to understand before asking for a camera. The axes are segment (club, high school, college, professional), sport (eight club sports each have their own page, and soccer and American football carry different tiers and different prices) and tier, billed per team per year at club level and per program per year at high school level [hf-25, hf-23, hf-05, hf-24]. Club soccer runs Core at 500 dollars (50 hours, livestreaming, sold only inside a club package), Plus at 1,000 (100 hours, AI summaries, positional stats, athlete profiles) and Premier at 2,500 (200 hours, scouting reports, analyst-supported breakdowns), with multi-team and club-wide packages quoted and discounted by up to 50 percent [hf-23]. US high schools pay 1,500, 2,500 or 4,000 dollars per program per year for Silver+, Gold+ and Platinum+, with Focus cameras and Hudl TV streaming excluded from all three and available only in the quoted Athletic Department package [hf-24]. The Focus camera itself never appears as a list price: the mid-market soccer Team Pack from 2,000 dollars is the one published bundle that includes a Flex, and the same page is served to UK visitors in dollars [hf-03, hf-04]. Fixed cameras are quote-only, with a 2022 US school board approving three at 3,000 dollars each inside an 11,000 dollar three-year contract and Hudl charging nothing for installation [hf-21, hf-07]; 2026 third-party guides repeat the 3,000 dollar figure and state that Hudl publishes no unit price [hf-22]. The practical consequence for a European club is that the camera is priced as a lever inside a multi-year software contract, so the number to negotiate is the package, and the per-team software price is where the money goes over five years.
criteria.support_service: All club tiers include email support and Gold adds game-time phone support, with a support portal and per-model user guides [hf-05, hf-07]. Warranty exists but its length is referred to the customer agreement, and Hudl says it reviews out-of-warranty failures [hf-06, hf-07]. Reviewers split between praising fantastic support and reporting reinstall advice for persistent connection failures [hf-15].
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Hudl is a private company founded in 2006 in Lincoln, Nebraska, backed by Accel, Nelnet, the Raikes family and Bain Capital Tech Opportunities since 2020, and it serves around 315,000 teams [hf-19, hf-23, hf-18]. It acquired Wyscout in 2019, Balltime in February 2025, Titan Sports in June 2025 and TeamUp in July 2026, and its 2025 to 2026 company news lists partnerships, grants and workplace awards without a single Focus product item [hf-19, hf-17]. The Flex launched in January 2023 with a four-hour battery and US 4G streaming, and the 2024 refresh is the last documented hardware change [hf-10, hf-09]. Financials are not public [hf-19].
criteria.evidence_references: Bromley FC's academy analysis lead is the named Flex reference, a Norwegian women's team appears in the Italian-language Flex article, and Hudl's US school deployments are documented in local board approvals [hf-11, hf-12, hf-21]. Hudl cites FC Barcelona among elite clients across its platform [hf-18]. No Italian Focus deployment is documented [hf-12].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: The Hudl Focus app holds 4.0 from 40 iOS ratings and 4.2 from 44 Google Play reviews, small samples that praise ease of use and support and criticise connection failures, repetitive setup screens and price [hf-15, hf-16]. Satisfaction with the wider Hudl platform is outside the scope of this record. Not assessable at scale from public sources.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Tracking runs on the camera, described as on-camera AI that pans and zooms, and film uploads in real time so that no cloud processing wait applies [hf-11, hf-02]. Fixed units buffer offline and upload later, and livestreams originate from the camera as RTMP [hf-08, hf-07]. Assist breakdowns are produced by Hudl analysts, with no automation involved [hf-03].
criteria.accessibility_languages: Hudl publishes Italian-language blog content for Focus Flex and runs Wyscout from Chiavari, and pricing pages for the UK market display in dollars [hf-12, hf-20, hf-04]. The 4G option is US-only, so European users rely on Wi-Fi or a hotspot [hf-06].
criteria.upgrade_path: A club can move from the Team Pack to the Coach and Analyst packs, adding Silver or Gold storage and Assist services, then to Sportscode, Wyscout and Titan within the same owner [hf-03, hf-05]. Fixed Indoor or Outdoor cameras add livestreaming and permanent coverage on a custom club-wide contract with multi-year terms [hf-05, hf-07]. The path stays inside Hudl, which is the point [hf-01].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the time from final whistle to film in the Hudl library over your own Wi-Fi, since instant availability is the core promise and connectivity is the main complaint [hf-02, hf-15]. Test the extra-wide tactical angle against a Veo panorama for the same match [hf-09]. Ask for the warranty length, the export terms for full matches and whether the Flex can livestream in your country before signing [hf-06, hf-01].

free.name: Once Sport (Once Sport d.o.o.)
free.payer_model_label: Club pays for a coaching tool
free.one_line: Desktop software from a Zagreb video analysis company that turns wide-angle footage from a Reolink camera, two GoPros or any panoramic source into an auto-followed broadcast-style video, with live streaming to YouTube and an optional €5 per match cloud processing service.
free.who_for: Coaches, analysts and small clubs that already own or can buy a cheap wide-angle camera and a reasonable PC, and who want automated match video for a few tens of euros a month, with no proprietary camera or locked cloud. Football academies in Portugal, Spain, Croatia, the UK and Italy make up the visible user base.
free.why: Once Sport exists because a video analysis software house realised that the expensive part of a Veo or Pixellot is the proprietary camera and cloud, and that a good tracking model running on the coach's own laptop could deliver the same virtual camera from commodity hardware [once-sport-01, once-sport-07]. It matters now because at €19 or €38 a month with hardware you source yourself, and €5 a match in the cloud, it undercuts every integrated system by an order of magnitude at the moment budgets at amateur clubs are being squeezed [once-sport-03]. It tells you that automated match video is being unbundled into camera, processing and platform, and that the processing layer is on its way to becoming a cheap software subscription.
free.price_band: €19/month Autocam Personal or €38/month Autocam Club, tax excluded, yearly billing at nine times the monthly rate; €5 per match cloud processing; camera hardware bought separately

italy.note: AS Lodigiani Calcio 1972 in Rome uses Autocam, Analyser and Coach Board across its academy and first team per a March 2025 case study, the software ships with an Italian interface and pricing table, and the company exhibited at The Coach Experience in Rimini in June 2025 [once-sport-08, once-sport-03, once-sport-06].
