verdict.look_if: You have someone at the club who is comfortable with a Windows PC, an SD card and a tripod, you already use or want Once Sport Analyser, and you want automated match video for a fraction of the cost of an integrated camera. Look also if privacy matters, since the offline version processes footage on your own computer and nothing leaves the building unless you stream it.
verdict.skip_if: You want a camera you bolt to a pole and forget, with someone else responsible when the recording fails, because Once Sport sells software and leaves hardware, mounting, power and connectivity to you. Skip also if you need fan monetisation, paywalls or sponsor management, or if your match video must be ready minutes after the final whistle without a capable PC on site.
watch_outs: Processing time on the offline version depends on your computer, and the Italian case study reports 65 to 70 minutes for a match, so budget for a decent GPU or use the €5 cloud option with a 24-hour turnaround [once-sport-08, once-sport-03].

Hardware is never included: the fixed option lists an 8K 20 fps IP67 camera with PoE and the portable option a 4K 20 fps IP67 camera or two action cameras on a 6-metre tripod, and Once Sport publishes no prices for any of it [once-sport-01].

Autocam Personal caps processing at 40 hours a month and three tagged football matches, and Autocam Club allows six tagged matches, so the automatic tagging component is metered even on the unlimited-hours plan [once-sport-03].
The 20 fps capture rate of the recommended cameras is below the 25 to 30 fps that broadcast-style output normally uses, which affects motion smoothness in the final video [once-sport-01].

The terms of service list Analyser and Coach Board by name and do not mention Autocam or the cloud processing service, and they place jurisdiction in England while stating the company is based in Croatia, so contractual coverage of match footage in the cloud tier is unclear [once-sport-04].
The company is a three-owner Croatian d.o.o. with no public financials, so support depth for a global user base of 5,000 or more claimed coaches rests on a small team [once-sport-09, once-sport-05].

criteria.use_case_fit: Autocam serves clubs that want automated match and training video from their own camera, on full-size and small-sided pitches from 5v5 to 11v11, across football, basketball, handball, futsal and more, with Analyser Basic and Coach Board bundled into the subscription since July 2025 [once-sport-01, once-sport-10]. Visible users are academies and semi-professional clubs such as HNK Vukovar 1991, ACD Carapeços and AS Lodigiani [once-sport-05, once-sport-11, once-sport-08]. It fits a coach-led workflow and does not fit a club that wants a hands-off streaming service.
criteria.capture_quality: Output quality depends on the source: the vendor's fixed recipe is an 8K, 20 fps, IP67 camera on PoE and the portable recipe a 4K, 20 fps, IP67 camera or two GoPro or DJI action cameras on a 6-metre tripod, with the software cropping a broadcast-style frame from the wide image [once-sport-01]. November 2025's version 3.0 added Reolink camera control and automatic stitching of two action cameras into one wide-angle source [once-sport-07]. Sample footage from Germany, the UK and Scotland is published on the Autocam page, and the 20 fps ceiling of the recommended cameras is the main quality constraint [once-sport-01].
criteria.automation_accuracy: The software uses neural networks and computer vision to digitally pan and zoom in imitation of a camera operator, with automatic field marking, tilt correction and adjustable zoom settings in the 3.0 processing setup [once-sport-01, once-sport-07]. Football matches can be automatically tagged, metered at three or six per month depending on plan [once-sport-03]. No accuracy figures or independent tests are published, and the Lodigiani analyst's description of television-like precision is the strongest public endorsement [once-sport-08].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Dual-camera processing stitches left and right action camera footage into a single wide-angle video without manual syncing, and the company offers a printable dual-GoPro mount design on request [once-sport-07, once-sport-01]. Single panoramic sources from Reolink are handled directly. There is no support for combining more than two sources or for cutting between separate angles.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Autocam can stream the processed feed live to YouTube or any RTMP platform while the match happens, with stream URL and key entered separately in the 3.0 interface, and live streaming to YouTube is included in both subscriptions [once-sport-01, once-sport-07, once-sport-03]. Live processing requires a capable computer at the pitch connected to the camera. The Portuguese club ACD Carapeços is presented as a live streaming case [once-sport-11]. No latency figure is published.
criteria.reliability_resilience: Because recording happens on the camera's SD card or the action cameras' storage and processing happens afterwards, a failed upload or PC crash does not lose the match footage [once-sport-07, once-sport-01]. Reliability of the recording itself depends on the user's hardware and setup. No app store ratings or independent reliability reviews exist, since the product is desktop software.
criteria.portability_install: The portable recipe is a 4K camera or two action cameras on a 6-metre tripod with a 12V power bank giving six hours and a waterproof bag, carried and set up by the club, and the Lodigiani academy uses this kit across home and away pitches [once-sport-01, once-sport-08]. The fixed recipe needs PoE and either the venue network or a router [once-sport-01]. Once Sport supplies instructions and software, the club supplies everything else.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Offline processing needs no internet at all, streaming needs a live uplink from the pitch-side PC, and the cloud tier needs the wide-angle file uploaded for a 24-hour turnaround [once-sport-01, once-sport-03]. No bandwidth figures are published. This is the least connectivity-dependent option in this group.
criteria.workflow_ux: The 3.0 release reorganised the desktop app into Source, Processing Setup and Destination tabs, with Reolink live preview, clip search and direct import, and processed video can be exported to any analysis platform [once-sport-07, once-sport-01]. Analyser Basic, Coach Board and, since December 2025, full Autocam integration inside Analyser reduce the number of tools a coach juggles [once-sport-10, once-sport-06]. It remains a desktop workflow that assumes a PC operator.
criteria.analysis_layer: Autocam subscriptions bundle Analyser Basic with professional tagging, telestration, basic automatic tracking, field mapping and basic export, and Coach Board for drills and tactical animation, with Analyser Pro at €36 and Elite at €72 a month as upgrades [once-sport-03, once-sport-10]. Automatic football tagging is metered per plan [once-sport-03]. Analyser is used by national teams, Dinamo Zagreb U19, Paris FC's women's centre and Arena Sport Slovenia, which gives the analysis layer stronger references than the camera layer [once-sport-05].
criteria.integrations: Processed video exports to any analysis platform, live output goes to YouTube and RTMP destinations, Reolink cameras are controlled natively and Coach Board projects exchange XML [once-sport-01, once-sport-07, once-sport-03]. Analyser imports CSV since November 2025 [once-sport-06]. There is no API and no club management or OTT integration.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is limited to a live stream to YouTube or another RTMP platform with sponsor logos and match results overlaid by Autocam [once-sport-01, once-sport-03]. There is no paywall, viewer app or highlight publishing product. Clubs monetise through their own YouTube channel or a third-party platform.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Footage stays on the club's camera storage and PC in the offline version, output is a standard video file, and the vendor states that videos remain private with offline functionality [once-sport-01]. The cloud per-match service requires uploading footage, and the published terms cover Analyser and Coach Board content rules without addressing Autocam cloud processing, retention or reuse [once-sport-04]. Ownership is strong in practice for offline users and undocumented for cloud users.
criteria.privacy_compliance: Offline processing means no personal data leaves the club unless it chooses to stream, which is the cleanest privacy posture in this group [once-sport-01]. The privacy policy covers account data and cookies, and there is no guidance on consent for filming minors or any blurring tool [once-sport-04]. Compliance for the footage itself therefore rests with the club.
criteria.security: Not assessable from public sources. The terms describe the company as based in Croatia and name no hosting provider or certification for the cloud service [once-sport-04].
criteria.pricing_tco: Autocam Personal is €19 a month or €171 a year and Autocam Club €38 a month or €342 a year, with yearly billing at nine times the monthly rate, USD equivalents of 23 and 46 a month, and cloud processing at €5 or USD 6 per match with packages such as 3+1 and 6+3, all tax excluded [once-sport-03]. Hardware is extra and unpriced by the vendor; a Reolink 8K PoE camera or two action cameras plus a 6-metre tripod and power bank are the stated inputs [once-sport-01]. A club buying its own kit can plausibly be running for under €1,000 in year one plus the subscription, which is the lowest entry cost among the vendors covered.
criteria.support_service: Support and updates are included in every subscription, a video analyst certification course comes with yearly plans, and the company runs a free trial and Calendly calls [once-sport-03, once-sport-01]. Testimonials praise the customer support team as very helpful [once-sport-05]. No SLA is published and the team is small.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Once Sport d.o.o. was founded in 2011 in Zagreb, is owned by Dalibor Čvek, Ivica Petrović and Nenad Markuš with Čvek and Markuš as directors, and publishes no financials [once-sport-09]. The blog shows a release roughly every month through 2025 and 2026, including Autocam 3.0 in November 2025, full Autocam integration into Analyser in December 2025 and a redesigned Coach Board and multitrack review in August 2026, alongside a heavy event schedule across Europe, the USA, Southeast Asia and Tunisia [once-sport-06, once-sport-07]. Cadence is the health signal; capital is unknown.
criteria.evidence_references: Autocam references include AS Lodigiani Calcio 1972 in Italy, HNK Vukovar 1991's academy, ACD Carapeços in Portugal and FC Ferreiras, while Analyser references include the Croatian national futsal team, Dinamo Zagreb U19, Paris FC, Plymouth Argyle, Greenock Morton, SK Interobal Plzeň, Estoril Praia, SV Sandhausen and FFF Pays de la Loire coach education [once-sport-05, once-sport-08, once-sport-11, once-sport-06]. The company claims 5,000 or more coaches, analysts and clubs worldwide [once-sport-05]. No independent test of Autocam output exists.
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Testimonials from analysts at Dinamo Zagreb, Paris FC, Sporting Braga and national team coaches praise ease of use, price and support, and the Lodigiani analyst calls Autocam revolutionary for combining automated recording with television-style framing [once-sport-05, once-sport-08]. These are vendor-selected quotes, and no third-party review site carries meaningful ratings. Sentiment is positive and thinly evidenced.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Autocam is edge by design, with processing on the club's own PC and an optional cloud tier at €5 per match for those without the hardware or the patience, and the choice is the customer's per match [once-sport-01, once-sport-03]. Processing time on the edge depends on the PC, with 65 to 70 minutes reported for a match in the Italian case [once-sport-08]. Live streaming requires the edge PC at the venue.
criteria.accessibility_languages: The software, pricing table and site run in English, German, French, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian, with a currency toggle between EUR and USD [once-sport-03, once-sport-01]. That makes Once Sport one of the few vendors in this database with a native Italian interface.
criteria.upgrade_path: A user can move from the €5 per match cloud tier to Personal to Club, add Analyser Pro or Elite and Coach Board Pro, and upgrade hardware from action cameras to a fixed 8K Reolink without changing software [once-sport-03, once-sport-01]. Plans can be upgraded or downgraded and cancelled on the pricing page terms [once-sport-02]. Software updates are included.
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Run the same match through the offline version on your own laptop and through the €5 cloud tier, compare output quality and time to delivery, and check the automatic football tagging against your own count [once-sport-03]. Test the dual-GoPro stitching on a small-sided pitch, since that is the cheapest possible entry [once-sport-07]. Confirm in writing what the cloud service does with uploaded footage, because the published terms do not say [once-sport-04].

free.name: Provispo B.V.
free.payer_model_label: Club pays for a coaching tool
free.one_line: A small Dutch integrator that installs fixed dual-camera panoramic and PTZ systems at professional training grounds, runs them from its PlayStats cloud, and has added a portable on-device 180-degree camera called SportCam Go for lower budgets.
free.who_for: Professional academies and federation training centres in the Benelux and Portugal that want owned camera infrastructure across several pitches, open export to Hudl, Sportscode or Nacsport, and RTSP feeds for live analysis. The SportCam Go targets amateur clubs and single-team analysts who want the same openness without the install.
free.why: Provispo exists because Dutch and Belgian academies wanted cameras that behaved like infrastructure they owned, with scheduled recording, local storage and plain MP4 downloads, with no closed subscription platform in the way, and a one-person Terneuzen company built that for Feyenoord, AZ, Genk and Royal Antwerp [provispo-01, provispo-03, provispo-09]. It matters now because the SportCam Go, with onboard processing, RTSP access and a 10-hour battery, takes that analyst-first, open-export philosophy into the portable segment where Veo and Pixellot sell closed clouds [provispo-02, provispo-08]. It tells you that the fight in this space is shifting from who has the best AI camera operator to who lets the club keep control of the footage and the workflow.
free.price_band: No prices published; all systems including SportCam Go are quoted after consultation

italy.note: No Italian client, reseller or office appears on the vendor site, in its news or in the company record, and the stated federation work covers the Netherlands, Belgium and Portugal [provispo-01, provispo-03].

verdict.look_if: You are an academy or federation with several pitches, an analyst on staff, existing Hudl, Sportscode, Nacsport or Dartfish licences, and a preference for owned hardware with open MP4 and RTSP access over a closed subscription cloud. Look at SportCam Go if you want a portable panoramic camera that processes on the device and can be used for live analysis without waiting for a cloud upload.
verdict.skip_if: You want published pricing, a large support organisation or a fan-facing streaming platform with paywall and sponsor tools, none of which Provispo offers. Skip also if you sit outside the Benelux and Portugal and need local installation and service, because the company is registered with one employee and has no stated presence elsewhere.
watch_outs: Provispo B.V. is registered with one employee at a Terneuzen address under RvL Holding B.V., so delivery depends on a very small team and its partners [provispo-09, provispo-10].
No price for any product, including SportCam Go, is published, and every enquiry goes through a WhatsApp or consultation route [provispo-02, provispo-01].
The SportCam Go page gives battery life, storage and field of view and omits resolution, weight, frame rate and tripod details [provispo-02].

Client and federation claims such as Feyenoord, AZ, Royal Antwerp, KRC Genk, the Belgian and Portuguese federations and the KNVB are stated by the vendor and could not be confirmed from the clubs' or federations' own channels [provispo-01, provispo-03].

The public news page carries a single item from October 2024, and the blog restarted in February 2026 with one comparison post and one password-protected Q&A, so public evidence of momentum is thin [provispo-07, provispo-11].
Livestreaming targets analysis tools and platforms such as Eyecons, YouTube, SportRecs and Vimeo, and there is no Provispo-owned OTT, paywall or sponsor overlay layer [provispo-05].

criteria.use_case_fit: The fixed SportCam Automatic pairs two cameras to record a full pitch in panoramic view with a tactical view and a fixed PTZ view for training zones, managed from PlayStats with scheduled recording and live tagging, and it is aimed at professional academies with named clients such as Royal Antwerp, Feyenoord, KRC Genk, Dinamo Zagreb, AZ Alkmaar and Excelsior [provispo-04, provispo-01]. SportCam Go extends the range to amateur clubs and single analysts with a portable 180-degree camera and an optional event data service [provispo-02]. Football is the stated core, with the site also listing golf, baseball, American football and combat sports features on third-party directories [provispo-12].
criteria.capture_quality: The vendor states 4K Ultra HD at up to 60 fps for its camera range, with the SportCam Side and SportCam Drone listed as 4K devices and the Goal camera giving a bird's-eye half-pitch view [provispo-01]. SportCam Go's resolution is not stated on its page, which gives only the 180-degree panoramic field of view, dual auto-follow and tactical feeds, 64 GB onboard storage and a 10-hour battery [provispo-02]. No sample footage specifications or independent tests are public.
criteria.automation_accuracy: Recording on the fixed system is driven by player and ball tracking with automated pan, tilt and zoom, and the software selects the tactical view automatically [provispo-04]. SportCam Go adds AI auto tracking that can be switched to manual control to focus on players or zones [provispo-02]. Provispo publishes no accuracy figures and there is no independent evaluation, so this is not assessable beyond vendor description.
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: The SportCam Recorder calibrates two side cameras capturing left and right halves of the pitch and uses that calibration for distance, position and speed measurements, then generates a combined output during recording [provispo-06]. Clubs can add Goal, Side, Control and Drone cameras under the same PlayStats management for multi-angle coverage [provispo-01, provispo-05]. SportCam Go stitches on the device into a single panorama with a separate auto-follow feed [provispo-02].
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live video from each SportCam is viewable in PlayStats during recording, RTSP and RTMP streams can be pushed straight into analysis suites, and SportCam Go offers RTSP and direct device access so analysis can start during the match without cloud processing [provispo-05, provispo-06, provispo-02]. Fan streaming goes to third-party platforms such as Eyecons, YouTube, SportRecs and Vimeo [provispo-05]. No latency figures are published.
criteria.reliability_resilience: The fixed system stores source video on the local disk of a PC workstation in a dedicated directory, which protects recordings from upload failures, and the cameras are described as weatherproof set-and-forget hardware [provispo-06, provispo-01]. SportCam Go records to 64 GB onboard storage on a 10-hour battery [provispo-02]. There are no public reliability reviews, app store ratings or uptime statements, so field reliability is not assessable from public sources.
criteria.portability_install: The core product is a permanent installation with two side cameras, a recorder workstation and optional additional cameras, which implies cabling and mounting at each pitch [provispo-06, provispo-04]. SportCam Go is placed beside the pitch and started with one button, with no tripod height or weight given [provispo-02]. Installation is presumably carried out by Provispo or partners in the Benelux, though the site does not say who installs.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: The fixed system records locally and uploads to PlayStats during or after the match, with Dotcomsport, Hudl and Soccerlab upload options integrated, so bandwidth needs are deferred to after the match [provispo-06]. SportCam Go processes on the device and offers RTSP over the local network, which means it works without an internet uplink at the pitch [provispo-02]. No minimum upload speeds are published.
criteria.workflow_ux: PlayStats handles camera management, scheduling from a mobile device, live viewing, real-time tagging with custom panels and shortcuts, clips and playlists, a zoomable player and MP4 download, and it imports XML, CSV and JSON event data from other providers to sync with video [provispo-05, provispo-04]. The workflow is built around an analyst at a desk. No app store listing was found for a Provispo mobile app.
criteria.analysis_layer: Provispo offers tagging, clips, playlists and import of third-party event data, plus an optional event data service on SportCam Go where clubs can have match events created for them [provispo-05, provispo-02]. The recorder's calibration supports distance, position and speed measurement from video [provispo-06]. There is no published metrics catalogue, no xG or physical reports and no API, so the analysis layer is a workflow tool that hands off to Hudl, Sportscode, Nacsport, Dartfish, MyVA or Longomatch [provispo-04, provispo-01].
criteria.integrations: Exports are plain MP4 for Nacsport, MyVA, Longomatch and Dartfish, uploads are integrated with Dotcomsport, Hudl and Soccerlab, live feeds go out over RTSP and RTMP, and PlayStats imports XML, CSV and JSON [provispo-04, provispo-06, provispo-05]. Openness to third-party tools is the company's stated positioning in its February 2026 comparison post [provispo-08]. This is the broadest documented integration set among the small European vendors.
criteria.distribution_ott: Livestreams can be sent to Eyecons, YouTube, SportRecs, Vimeo and similar platforms for fan engagement, and that is the extent of distribution [provispo-05]. There is no Provispo viewer app, paywall, sponsor banner tool or highlight publishing product. Clubs wanting monetised streaming need a separate platform.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Source video sits on the club's own workstation for the fixed system, all recordings are also stored in the PlayStats cloud with preview and download, and SportCam Go keeps footage on the device with direct access [provispo-06, provispo-05, provispo-02]. No terms of service, privacy policy or data licence could be found on the public site, so ownership and reuse rights are undocumented in public. The architecture favours the club, the paperwork is invisible.
criteria.privacy_compliance: No privacy policy, consent guidance, blurring feature or data processing terms are published on the site, and the only privacy-related feature is offline, on-device processing on SportCam Go [provispo-02]. For a Dutch B.V. serving academies with minors this is a documentation gap, and practice may be better. Not assessable from public sources.
criteria.security: Not assessable from public sources. The site documents no hosting region, certification or access control for PlayStats.
criteria.pricing_tco: No price is published for any camera, the recorder, PlayStats or SportCam Go, and the site routes every enquiry to a consultation, a WhatsApp chat or a gated white paper [provispo-02, provispo-01]. A fixed dual-camera install with a workstation and cloud platform will sit in professional academy budgets; SportCam Go is positioned for amateur clubs, which implies a price below the fixed system, and nothing more can be said without a quote. Total cost therefore cannot be modelled from public material.
criteria.support_service: Support is offered through email, a Dutch mobile number and WhatsApp with a claim of 24/7 availability and replies within minutes, and the named team is three people: CEO Remco van Leeuwen, sales manager Marc Verwei and operational manager Dennis de Kraker [provispo-01, provispo-03]. The company record shows one employee, so the wider team likely works through the holding or as contractors [provispo-09]. No SLA is published.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Provispo B.V. (KvK 76830462) dates from October 2010, is owned by RvL Holding B.V. since December 2019, is registered under SBI 62100 computer programming with one employee, and files no public financial detail [provispo-09, provispo-10]. Public activity in 2025 and 2026 consists of the SportCam Go launch, a February 2026 comparison post and a protected Q&A on an AI-powered Goal camera, plus the FC Twente injury research partnership from October 2024 [provispo-02, provispo-11, provispo-07]. The company claims more than a decade of operation and 100 intelligent systems deployed [provispo-03].
criteria.evidence_references: Vendor-stated references include Royal Antwerp, Feyenoord, KRC Genk, Standard Liège, Dinamo Zagreb, AZ Alkmaar, Excelsior Rotterdam, FC Twente and the Dutch, Belgian and Portuguese federations, with headline numbers of 3 or more federations, 95 or more clubs (45 professional, 50 amateur), 100 systems and 10,000 or more matches captured [provispo-01, provispo-03]. The FC Twente research collaboration with Demcon Johan Sports and the University of Twente is the one dated, named partnership announcement [provispo-07]. None of the club or federation references could be confirmed from the counterparties' own channels.
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: No independent reviews, app store ratings or case study quotes from analysts are public, and the SourceForge listing shows zero reviews [provispo-12]. Not assessable from public sources.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: The fixed system is edge first, recording to a local workstation and syncing to PlayStats later, and SportCam Go processes entirely on the device with RTSP access and no cloud dependency, which the vendor presents as a deliberate contrast with cloud-processing competitors [provispo-06, provispo-02]. PlayStats is the cloud layer for storage, tagging and sharing [provispo-05]. This is the most edge-oriented architecture in this group.
criteria.accessibility_languages: The website is in English with Dutch-language contact details, and the company operates in the Netherlands, Belgium and Portugal [provispo-01, provispo-03]. No Italian, French or German interface or support is documented.
criteria.upgrade_path: A club can start with SportCam Go, move to a fixed SportCam Automatic install, and add Goal, Side, Control and Drone cameras under one PlayStats account, with an AI-powered Goal camera previewed in a February 2026 Q&A [provispo-01, provispo-11]. Because exports are MP4 and RTSP, the upgrade path does not lock the club into Provispo's platform. No firmware or roadmap communication is public.
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the RTSP feed from SportCam Go into your existing analysis suite on the bench and measure how quickly you can start tagging during the first half [provispo-02]. Test the MP4 download and XML import round trip with your current provider's event data in PlayStats [provispo-05]. Ask for a written price, a written data licence and the names of two academy clients you can call, since none of the three exists in public.

free.name: Reeplayer
free.payer_model_label: Club pays for a coaching tool
free.one_line: Reeplayer sells a US made three lens soccer camera with on device AI and a built in SIM for USD 1,499 plus USD 99 a month, streams every game live for free, and since July 2026 offers to give teams the camera when a local brand sponsors it [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-05].
free.who_for: American youth and amateur soccer teams that want instant livestreams and quick uploads without a parent managing hotspots or ethernet cables, and club directors willing to try an advertising funded camera [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-06]. The company states it is available only in the United States and only for soccer [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-03].
free.why: Reeplayer exists because a Los Angeles founding team decided the cure for slow uploads and dead hotspots was a camera with its own cellular modem and an NVIDIA Jetson doing the AI on the sideline, and it raised USD 10 million in 2023 to build that in Pittsburgh [reeplayer-08, reeplayer-10]. It matters now because the July 2026 End Pay-to-Play initiative tries to move the bill from families to brands, with 40% of advertising profit returned to the team, which is the first serious attempt in this market to turn the camera from a cost into a media asset [reeplayer-05, reeplayer-06]. It tells you that whoever controls the livestream of youth games controls an audience, and that vendors are starting to price accordingly.
free.price_band: USD 1,499 camera + USD 349 tripod one off, plus USD 1,188/yr (USD 99/month billed annually) or USD 2,700 per three years; sponsor funded option at USD 0 to the team where a brand signs

italy.note: Reeplayer states the product is exclusively available in the United States and the built in data plan is tied to US carriers, so there is no Italian or European availability [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-03].

free.evidence_note: Pricing, features and availability are verified from Reeplayer's own pages; hardware architecture comes from the manufacturing partner Hellbender; funding and the sponsorship model come from trade press and Crunchbase; camera resolution and independent reliability data are not published.

verdict.look_if: You run a US soccer club and value a livestream that starts without any phone or router, uploads in 5 to 30 minutes and has no per user or per viewer fees [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-04]. You are open to a local sponsor paying for the camera in exchange for exclusive advertising on your team's stream [reeplayer-06].
verdict.skip_if: You are outside the United States, since sales, cellular coverage and support are US only [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-03]. You need a proven analysis layer, because auto tagging is still described as planned and the App Store reviews flag tracking loss on long passes and free kicks [reeplayer-04, reeplayer-07].
watch_outs: The camera and tripod are a USD 1,848 upfront purchase and the subscription is billed annually or every three years, so first year cost is about USD 3,184 with the case and mount [reeplayer-01].

Camera resolution is not published anywhere on Reeplayer's site or in the Hellbender case study, and the company markets HD uploads and pixel density without giving a number [reeplayer-03, reeplayer-08, reeplayer-10].

The sponsor funded model had one committed brand covering four Southern California teams and a second brand pending in Arizona as of July 2026, with cameras due in August 2026, so it is a pilot at this stage [reeplayer-05].
App Store reviewers report the AI missing significant moments and no manual pan to recover when tracking fails [reeplayer-07].
Crunchbase lists 1 to 10 employees, which is small for a company running hardware, cellular contracts and an advertising sales effort [reeplayer-09].

criteria.use_case_fit: Reeplayer is a team level soccer camera for the United States with unlimited teams, games and users on one subscription, and its public reference logos include Sporting Kansas City, UCLA and the Brazilian federation [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-03]. Its mission page frames the product around getting young athletes discovered, which places it between a coaching tool and a family streaming service [reeplayer-03]. The sponsorship model targets pay to play youth clubs specifically [reeplayer-06].
criteria.capture_quality: The camera carries three Sony sensors covering left, centre and right of the field, stitched and processed on an NVIDIA Jetson module, with integrated microphones [reeplayer-10, reeplayer-08]. Reeplayer argues three sensors give higher pixel density for digital zoom and does not state output resolution [reeplayer-10]. App Store reviewers praise video quality while criticising framing choices [reeplayer-07].
criteria.automation_accuracy: Player detection and highlight creation run on device using jersey number tracking, according to the manufacturing partner [reeplayer-08]. Reviewers say ball tracking is unreliable on long passes and free kicks and that the AI occasionally misses key moments [reeplayer-07]. Automatic tagging of goals, fouls and cards is listed as a planned feature [reeplayer-04].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Three fixed lenses are stitched into one panoramic view from which the AI pans and zooms, so there is a single virtual camera output [reeplayer-08, reeplayer-04]. No separate angle selection for viewers is documented.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live streaming is included with unlimited viewers via a shareable link, uses the built in SIM to pick the strongest carrier automatically and adapts bitrate to bandwidth [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-04]. Streams go to Reeplayer's own viewer platform and to YouTube and other platforms [reeplayer-08]. Latency is not published.
criteria.reliability_resilience: The camera records up to four hours per charge, can charge while operating, stores up to 30 games locally and is ruggedised for outdoor use [reeplayer-04, reeplayer-08]. Instant playback works right after the game before upload completes, which protects against connectivity failures [reeplayer-03]. No public failure statistics or Trustpilot presence exist.
criteria.portability_install: The unit is tripod mounted and portable, with a USD 349 tripod, a USD 49 tilt mount and a USD 99 Nanuk case sold alongside [reeplayer-01]. No installation is required and camera management is remote through the app [reeplayer-03].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: A built in SIM with a data plan included in the subscription connects to AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon automatically, and WiFi upload is also available [reeplayer-10, reeplayer-04]. HD games upload in 5 to 30 minutes depending on connection [reeplayer-03]. This removes the hotspot dependency that Trace and XbotGo carry.
criteria.workflow_ux: The app supports unlimited team profiles, permissions per user, clipping, MP4 downloads of full games and highlights, custom moment tags, comments and player profiles [reeplayer-04]. The iOS app is rated 4.4 from 18 ratings with praise for ease of use and responsive support [reeplayer-07]. The last App Store update visible was version 3.3.5 in July 2025 [reeplayer-07].
criteria.analysis_layer: Coaches can create custom tags such as goals, saves and tactical examples and share them with the team, and AI auto tagging and natural language search are planned [reeplayer-04]. There are no drawing tools, fitness data or tactical statistics, so this is a video sharing tool and the analysis suite is still to come.
criteria.integrations: Livestreams can be pushed to YouTube and other platforms [reeplayer-08]. An affiliate programme exists for referrals [reeplayer-06]. No API or third party analysis export is documented.
criteria.distribution_ott: Reeplayer runs its own viewer platform with free public access, no viewer limits and, under End Pay-to-Play, exclusive brand sponsorship on a team's camera feed targetable by city, zip code or neighbourhood [reeplayer-04, reeplayer-06]. Sponsors are promised about 36 hours a year of exposure per viewing family [reeplayer-05]. This is the only vendor in this group with an advertising layer on grassroots streams.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Full games, clips and highlights download as MP4 files with no stated limits, and cloud storage is included in the subscription [reeplayer-04, reeplayer-01]. Retention after cancellation and ownership of footage used in sponsored streams are not published.
criteria.privacy_compliance: Reeplayer offers audio muting on any footage and permission controls per user, and does not document blurring, opt out for players or a policy on minors [reeplayer-04]. Sponsored livestreams place children's games in front of advertisers, and the public material does not explain what consent is collected from families or opponents [reeplayer-06]. Data residency is US by default and irrelevant to EU buyers since the product is not sold there [reeplayer-01].
criteria.pricing_tco: Hardware is USD 1,499 for the camera and USD 349 for the tripod, with a USD 99 case and USD 49 mount optional, and the subscription is USD 99 a month billed annually or USD 75 a month on a three year contract, giving a first year total of USD 3,184 and USD 5,063 over three years by Reeplayer's own arithmetic [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-10]. Cellular data, livestreaming and unlimited users are included, and there is a 14 day money back guarantee and 6 to 24 month payment plans [reeplayer-01]. Under End Pay-to-Play a sponsored team pays nothing and receives 40% of advertising profits [reeplayer-06].
criteria.support_service: Support is US based with a help centre, and reviewers describe customer service as responsive [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-07]. Hours and SLAs are not published.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Reeplayer, Inc. was founded in 2021 by Orhan Basak Ajredinovski with four co founders and raised USD 10 million in a venture round led by Keiretsu Forum Turkey in August 2023 [reeplayer-09, reeplayer-11]. Hardware is manufactured by Hellbender in Pittsburgh with hundreds of systems deployed [reeplayer-08]. The July 2026 sponsorship pivot, with a goal of fully offsetting player fees for participating teams by 2030, is the current strategic bet, and headcount is listed at 1 to 10 [reeplayer-05, reeplayer-09].
criteria.evidence_references: Reeplayer shows logos for Sporting Kansas City, UCLA Bruins, Liverpool and the Brazilian federation CBF without describing the deployments [reeplayer-03]. Hellbender reports hundreds of systems and thousands of games captured [reeplayer-08]. Sponsored deployments cover four Southern California teams as of July 2026 [reeplayer-05].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: The iOS app holds 4.4 out of 5 from 18 ratings with positive comments on ease of use, clip sharing and support and negative comments on tracking during long passes and open field play [reeplayer-07]. The sample is small and no coach or analyst review from a club is public.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Detection, tracking and highlight creation run on the camera's NVIDIA Jetson during recording, which is why playback is instant and uploads are short, with cloud used for storage, sharing and streaming distribution [reeplayer-08, reeplayer-03].
criteria.accessibility_languages: English only, US only [reeplayer-01]. No accessibility features are documented.
criteria.upgrade_path: Teams can move from an annual to a three year plan at a lower monthly rate, add teams and users without extra cost and, where a sponsor signs, convert to the sponsor funded model [reeplayer-01, reeplayer-06]. Auto tagging and natural language search are announced future features [reeplayer-04].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the built in cellular livestream at a rural or crowded venue where hotspots fail, since that is the core design claim [reeplayer-04]. Time the upload after a 90 minute game against the 5 to 30 minute claim [reeplayer-03]. If considering sponsorship, ask for the advertising profit definition behind the 40% share and what families are told about advertising on their children's games [reeplayer-06].

free.name: Spiideo
free.payer_model_label: Club pays for a coaching tool
free.one_line: Spiideo installs cloud-connected fixed cameras (S-Line, X-Line, D-Line, A-Line) on pitches and arenas and sells a cloud suite on top, led by Spiideo Perform for coaches and analysts and Spiideo Play for automated live production, with Replay, League Exchange, AutoData and OTT alongside [sp-08, sp-19].
free.who_for: Professional and semi-professional clubs, academies, universities and leagues that want permanent multi-pitch capture with no server on site and a shared video and data workflow, with the A-Line announced for pre-order in March 2026 as the cheaper route for smaller venues [sp-09, sp-03, sp-14]. Grassroots teams with one pitch and one camera budget are served better by the portable vendors, since Spiideo publishes no list price and sells by quote [sp-19, sp-08].
free.why: The Roma case shows the pattern Spiideo is built for: a club with several pitches that wants the whole training ground recorded every day, where a PoE camera feeding a cloud platform removes both the operator and the on-site server [sp-14, sp-07, sp-09]. It matters now because revenue reached 243 million Swedish kronor in 2025 with losses still at 56 million, a 20 million dollar round in 2024 and the Signality tracking acquisition point to a company buying its way into data, and AI Highlights in May 2026 shows production automation moving from camera control to editorial [sp-06, sp-01, sp-02, sp-04]. My reading is that the space is splitting, with one camp selling cheap capture to amateurs and Spiideo betting that leagues, federations and academies will pay for capture, data and broadcast in one cloud, which is the audience its 2026 launches name [sp-04].
free.price_band: Quote-only; the one published partner price is USD 1,875 per team package for 25 games with AutoData stats and 50 hours of storage in a US hockey programme, and Spiideo claims the A-Line is up to 44 percent cheaper than comparable systems

italy.note: AS Roma automates capture on four training pitches with Spiideo Perform, the Milan youth academy SSD Ausonia 1931 installed cameras on three pitches on Inter's recommendation, Inter Milan is named as a customer by Sportico, and Spiideo lists Italy as a remote office location and offers Italian on its support site [sp-14, sp-15, sp-22, sp-16, sp-23].

verdict.look_if: You run an academy or club with several pitches, a full-time analyst and a stadium or arena where live production with graphics and replay is part of the plan, and you want no server on site [sp-14, sp-18]. You are a league or conference that wants a video exchange, replay for officials and automated production across many venues on one contract [sp-05, sp-19].
verdict.skip_if: You want to know the price before talking to sales, because Spiideo publishes no list price and the only public figure is a US hockey partner package [sp-13]. You want a portable camera you can carry to away matches for under 1,500 euros, since the Portable SmartCam weighs under eight kilograms and sits inside the same quote-based model [sp-10].
watch_outs: Custom downloads with a chosen view, including the panorama, require the Pro Plus tier, take around 20 minutes to render and expire after seven days [sp-12].
The A-Line needs PoE+ at 30 watts, a cabled connection and at least 15 megabits per second of upload per camera, so pitch cabling is part of the project [sp-07].

The public privacy policy dates from June 2022, names Spiideo as controller for its own users and says nothing about people filmed, hosting region, sub-processors or a data processing agreement [sp-17].
The company lost 55.7 million kronor in 2025 on 243.3 million of revenue and equity fell from 180.7 million to 127.0 million kronor during the year [sp-06].
The Spiideo consumer app has nine App Store ratings, several of which describe frozen paid streams, so the fan-facing layer is thin compared with the coaching layer [sp-21].
The 44 percent cheaper claim for the A-Line has no published reference price attached to it [sp-03].

criteria.use_case_fit: Spiideo sells to professional clubs, academies, universities and leagues, with AS Roma, Brentford, Livingston and San Diego Loyal as named football users and the NBA, NHL, Premier League and NCAA among its markets [sp-19, sp-22]. The product set covers analysis (Perform), production (Play with CloudStudio), officiating (Replay), video exchange (League Exchange) and data (AutoData) [sp-19]. Youth academies such as Ausonia 1931 in Milan and IFK Stocksund use it for multi-pitch training capture and streamed matches [sp-15, sp-19].
criteria.capture_quality: The S-Line mark III records multiple 4K streams at up to 50 or 60 frames per second (the higher frame rates require the Perform Pro Plus tier) with a larger sensor claimed to double low-light performance and a 170 degree view, and the X-Line uses Canon optics with 4K per camera and IP66 or IP67 protection [sp-09, sp-08]. The A-Line captures at 2K with a 180 degree panorama, optical zoom and 25 or 30 frames per second from 3 to 20 metres off the sideline [sp-08, sp-03]. The Portable SmartCam offers an ultra-wide 180 degree view over Wi-Fi or 4G [sp-10].
criteria.automation_accuracy: AutoFollow tracking is tuned for more than 15 sports and Perform offers fixed, panorama, standard, wide, all-players and custom-area follow views for the same recording [sp-18, sp-12]. The Signality acquisition added optical tracking and real-time data generation, and Spiideo has not stated which tracking feeds AutoData or the AI Highlights product launched in May 2026 [sp-02, sp-04]. Spiideo publishes no accuracy metrics, and coach testimonials speak to time saved and say nothing about tracking precision [sp-14, sp-19].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Perform lets users choose which camera angle to download when several cameras cover one scene, and CloudStudio switches between AI cameras and third-party cameras, drones and manual feeds in one production [sp-12, sp-18]. The D-Line uses triple camera sensors with built-in stitching and Virtual Panorama gives full-field coverage [sp-08, sp-14]. Of the fixed-camera vendors in this scan, this is the widest published multi-angle capability, which is my comparison of the vendor pages and no vendor's claim.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Spiideo Play with CloudStudio produces live with instant replay, commentary, data-triggered graphics, region-specific branding, clean feeds and a low-latency option for sportsbooks [sp-18]. Commentator Mode added in August 2026 gives commentators the produced feed and control of their microphone [sp-05]. The camera page quotes a 3-second low-latency feed and RTMP/SRT output, Spiideo publishes no end-to-end latency for produced streams, and the consumer app reviews report freezing on paid streams [sp-08, sp-18, sp-21].
criteria.reliability_resilience: Cameras are outbound-only devices on DHCP that need HTTPS, NTP and a short list of TCP and UDP ports, and Spiideo says systems update themselves with no local server [sp-07, sp-09]. Spiideo claims more than 7,000 arenas and conference-scale replay deployments across 12 Southland institutions now in their second season [sp-04, sp-05]. No uptime figures or status page were found [sp-23].
criteria.portability_install: Fixed lines connect by Ethernet up to 100 metres, fibre up to 1,000 metres or a line-of-sight wireless link, and the A-Line runs on a single PoE+ cable with surge protection advised in lightning-prone areas [sp-24, sp-07]. The Portable SmartCam weighs under eight kilograms and sets up in under ten minutes [sp-10]. Installation is a cabling project, which is the price of permanent daily capture [sp-24].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: The A-Line needs at least 15 megabits per second upload per camera or footage is delayed or downgraded [sp-07]. Fixed cameras need Ethernet, fibre or a line-of-sight wireless link back to the network, and the portable unit uses Wi-Fi or 4G with 5G announced [sp-24, sp-10]. Everything uploads to the cloud, so a multi-pitch site needs upload capacity sized for concurrent sessions, which is arithmetic from the 15 megabit figure and no Spiideo statement [sp-07].
criteria.workflow_ux: Perform offers tagging, smart search, clip collections, opponent scouting, presentations and, in 2026, a tag length editor and auto-notes on tags [sp-13, sp-05]. Downloads are standalone H.264 MP4 files across tiers with view selection reserved to Pro Plus [sp-12]. Brentford reports saving 10 to 12 hours per week and Roma reports removing 10 hours of sideline filming weekly [sp-19, sp-14].
criteria.analysis_layer: AutoData provides advanced statistics per game, priced in the Black Bear hockey programme at 75 dollars per game inside a 1,875 dollar 25-game package for the 2024-25 season [sp-13]. Spiideo acquired the optical-tracking firm Signality in December 2024 and said its data generation would be integrated into Spiideo's products, without saying how AutoData changed [sp-02]. Perform tiers run League Exchange, Lite, Pro and Pro Plus with feature matrices published as images, so they cannot be searched or copied [sp-11].
criteria.integrations: Spiideo runs a developer portal with an API reference and authentication guide, and its AI Highlights were built with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center on Amazon Bedrock [sp-20, sp-04]. CloudStudio ingests third-party cameras and delivers clean feeds to partners [sp-18]. The camera page mentions export to third-party analysis software and RTMP/SRT output without naming partners, and no named integration with Hudl Sportscode or Wyscout appears on the clubs page [sp-08, sp-19].
criteria.distribution_ott: Spiideo Play includes an OTT service with payment integration and sponsor placement, and RED.Sport Network covers more than 50 leagues on it [sp-19, sp-18]. The IWSOC National Video Exchange for more than 350 NCAA Division I women's soccer programmes went live in August 2026 with Spiideo as provider [sp-05]. AI Highlights packages clips for different platforms as an add-on to Play [sp-04].
criteria.data_access_ownership: Downloads produce a standalone MP4 with the chosen view, but custom downloads are limited to Pro Plus subscribers and expire after seven days [sp-12]. The privacy policy states business data is kept for the duration of the agreement, and no public terms describe what happens to footage after termination [sp-17]. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.privacy_compliance: The public privacy policy, last updated 7 June 2022, treats Spiideo AB as controller for account holders and marketing contacts and does not address people appearing in footage, minors, hosting region, transfer mechanisms or a data processing agreement [sp-17]. No blurring, consent or opt-out tooling was found on the help centre's collection index [sp-23]. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.security: Spiideo documents outbound-only camera traffic on specific ports and cloud-hosted processing, and its AI Highlights run on AWS services [sp-07, sp-04]. No SOC 2, ISO 27001, penetration test statement or security page was found on the public site [sp-23]. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.pricing_tco: Spiideo sells by quote, and the one public package is 1,875 dollars per team for 25 games with AutoData and 50 hours of storage through Black Bear Sports Group in US hockey [sp-13]. The A-Line is positioned as up to 44 percent cheaper than comparable solutions without a reference price [sp-03]. Budget for PoE+ switching, cabling and 15 megabits of upload per camera on top of the subscription [sp-07].
criteria.support_service: The help centre runs in English, French, German, Italian, Polish, Spanish and Swedish and links to a training library called the Spiideo Academy [sp-23]. No support hours, SLAs or warranty terms are published [sp-23]. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Spiideo AB, registered 556883-4435, grew revenue from 74.2 million kronor in 2021 to 243.3 million in 2025 while losing between 38.4 and 72.2 million kronor every year, with equity of 127.0 million kronor at the end of 2025 [sp-06]. It raised 20 million dollars in June 2024 led by Cipio Partners with Mathias Kamprad, taking total funding to 40 million dollars, acquired Signality in December 2024 and was named to the Sifted 100 Nordics list in September 2026 [sp-01, sp-02, sp-05]. Product cadence in 2026 shows the A-Line, AI Highlights, Commentator Mode, auto-notes and the tag length editor [sp-03, sp-04, sp-05].
criteria.evidence_references: AS Roma automates four training pitches and quotes its video analyst on workflow gains, and Ausonia 1931 in Milan installed three pitches on Inter's recommendation [sp-14, sp-15]. Brentford, Livingston and San Diego Loyal are named football users and the Southland Conference runs replay across 12 institutions and seven sports [sp-19, sp-05]. Spiideo claims more than 7,000 arenas, more than 4,000 organisations and around 200 employees in 12 countries [sp-04, sp-16].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Named analysts at Roma and Brentford report large weekly time savings [sp-14, sp-19]. Public review volume is negligible, with nine App Store ratings averaging 4.3 and the written reviews mostly fan complaints about frozen paid streams [sp-21]. Not assessable at scale from public sources.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: All cameras are cloud-connected with no local server; AI Highlights runs on AWS, and Spiideo does not say where AutoFollow and AutoData are hosted [sp-09, sp-04]. Cameras upload continuously and lower image quality when upload speed is short, so the site link is the bottleneck [sp-07]. Replay for officials runs from the same cloud with remote collaboration to on-field officials [sp-28].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The help centre and support run in seven languages including Italian, and Spiideo lists Italy as a remote office location with staff in 12 countries [sp-23, sp-16]. Around half of revenue comes from North America [sp-01].
criteria.upgrade_path: Spiideo's tiers (Lite, Pro, Pro Plus) and add-ons suggest a path from a single A-Line with Perform to full live production with Play and CloudStudio and Replay for officials on the same cameras, but no published upgrade path or per-game AutoData pricing exists outside partner deals [sp-11, sp-13, sp-18]. Leagues use the League Exchange tier and can add AI Highlights as a Play add-on [sp-11, sp-04]. The path runs inside one cloud account, which in my reading is the main argument for paying more up front.
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the custom-area AutoFollow and multi-angle download on a training session, because that is where the fixed multi-camera design pays off [sp-12]. Test AI Highlights on a full match and judge whether the story cuts are publishable without an editor [sp-04]. Ask for the price of the A-Line against a Veo Cam 3 plus Club plan and check the 44 percent claim [sp-03].

free.why: Veo exists because grassroots clubs wanted the analysis habit of professional football without the staff, and a 1,299 euro camera plus a 579 to 1,159 euro yearly plan made that habit affordable [veo-02]. It matters now because the company has crossed 500 million Danish kroner in revenue and cut its annual loss to under 5 million kroner in 2025, which puts it closer to breakeven than any other portable camera vendor whose accounts I have read [veo-08]. The Lega Nazionale Dilettanti partnership of September 2025 and the free Analytics 2 bundle running to 30 September 2026 show where the space is going, with hardware treated as a loss leader and the money made on data and analytics add-ons [veo-11, veo-05].

verdict.look_if: You run a club with one to ten teams, you want match video available in the app the same evening with automatic highlights, and you are willing to own the camera and pay per camera per year [veo-04, veo-02]. Italian LND-affiliated clubs should look now, because the current bundle gives away the camera or the Analytics 2 add-on on a 12-month Team plan, which turns the first year into a 929 euro decision [veo-05, veo-12].
verdict.skip_if: You need live streaming as the core product, because Veo Live is an add-on that pushes RTMP to YouTube or Facebook and the fan app shows freezing complaints in reviews [veo-04, veo-20]. You need to export the panoramic master or tracking data for your own analysis pipeline, because downloads are limited to the follow-cam MP4 and Analytics data cannot be exported [veo-23].
watch_outs: Only the follow-cam view can be downloaded, the panoramic and interactive views and all Analytics data stay inside the platform, so ownership of your footage is narrower than it looks [veo-23].
The Starter plan runs six months of storage and excludes downloads, so a club that stops paying loses access to its archive [veo-04, veo-23].
The free-repair window is one year from delivery, after which battery repairs cost 200 euros and other components 350 euros, and a triggered G-force meter voids the claim [veo-18].
Trustpilot shows 34 percent one-star reviews out of 1,282, with recurring complaints about auto-renewal charges after cancellation and slow support escalation [veo-21].

Veo acts as processor only, so the club is the data controller and carries the consent burden for filming minors, and Veo documents no blurring or opt-out tooling for people on the pitch [veo-14, veo-17].
The Italian promotion price for the Cam 3 plus Analytics 2 bundle is rendered as a placeholder on the page, so confirm the invoice total against the catalogue prices before signing [veo-05, veo-02].

criteria.use_case_fit: Veo is built for the club that films its own matches and training with no operator and reviews them in the Veo Editor, with plans sized from one team and 15 users on Starter to 20 teams and 600 users on Enterprise [veo-04, veo-02]. Football is the primary sport with automatic event detection for goals, shots, corners and free kicks, and Analytics 2 is football only [veo-24, veo-04]. Schools and multi-sport programs are served with US-only School plans at 2,499 and 2,999 dollars per year [veo-01].
criteria.capture_quality: Veo Cam 3 records two synchronised streams stitched to a 180 degree panorama and outputs a 1080p follow-cam, with an interactive mode that lets the viewer pan and zoom the full pitch [veo-06]. The camera weighs 1.25 kilograms, carries 96.81 gigabytes of internal storage and runs up to 6.5 hours recording or 4.5 hours recording plus live streaming on one charge, within a stated operating range of minus 10 to 45 degrees Celsius [veo-07]. Veo Go relies on the ultra-wide sensors of two iPhone 11 or newer handsets and needs roughly 6 gigabytes of phone storage per hour per phone [veo-22].
criteria.automation_accuracy: The follow-cam and event detection run in Veo's cloud AI pipeline after upload, which is described in the data processing agreement as stitching, follow-cam, interactive mode and game event detection [veo-17]. Veo publishes no accuracy figures, and App Store reviewers report analytics data that misses moments when checked against possession statistics and a zoom that stays wider than coaches want [veo-19]. Trustpilot reviews from 2026 describe the automatic tracking as working well for the typical amateur match [veo-21].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: The system is a single two-lens unit that stitches one panorama, so there is no multi-camera production and no second angle behind the goal in the product line [veo-06]. Veo Go combines two separate iPhones into one panoramic field view with follow-cam, which is the closest Veo comes to multi-device capture [veo-22].
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live streaming requires the Veo Live add-on, priced from 119 euros per year on Starter to 469 euros per year on Enterprise in Italy, and pushes to YouTube, Facebook or any RTMP endpoint [veo-02, veo-04]. The 5G camera variant at 1,599 euros takes a nano SIM for streaming without Wi-Fi [veo-02, veo-06]. Veo publishes no latency figures, and the fan-facing Veo Live app has 13,000 ratings at 4.8 stars with a visible minority reporting streams that freeze after a minute or two [veo-20].
criteria.reliability_resilience: The Veo Cam app holds 4.7 stars from 1,500 ratings with reviewers reporting whole seasons without failures, alongside individual reports of overheating and of an APN settings button that does not respond [veo-19]. Trustpilot carries battery drain complaints and a refurbished replacement path exists at 579 euros for a Cam 3 and 749 euros for the 5G model when repair fails after year one [veo-21, veo-18, veo-02]. Recording is local to the camera with upload once connected, so a dropped connection during the match does not lose the file [veo-06].
criteria.portability_install: The camera mounts on a 5.2 metre tripod at 249 euros or a 7.4 metre tripod at 399 euros, with a 149 euro stadium mount package for permanent positions and a 89 euro travel case [veo-02]. Setup is a tripod-and-record workflow with no cabling, and an Ethernet dongle is sold separately for fixed installs [veo-07]. Veo Go needs only the 39 euro tripod and the 20 euro phone rig, both included free on yearly Go plans [veo-02, veo-22].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Veo Cam 3 uploads over Wi-Fi or a phone hotspot, the 5G variant adds a cellular modem, and Ethernet works through an adaptor [veo-07]. Veo publishes no minimum upload bandwidth, and processing time is described only as dependent on connection and match length [veo-06]. Recording hours per month are capped by plan at 10 hours on Starter, 20 on Team and 200 on Club, which sets the practical upload budget [veo-04].
criteria.workflow_ux: The Veo Editor offers automatic clips for shots and goals, manual clips and bookmarks, drawing tools, a speedrun mode that skips dead time, player of the match, timelines and journals, in English, Italian, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Polish [veo-24]. Reviewers praise setup and ease of use and criticise player selection that cannot group users and the removal of an in-app feedback tool in version 3.2.10 [veo-21, veo-19]. The platform runs in the browser at app.veo.co plus iOS apps for camera control and viewing [veo-23, veo-24].
criteria.analysis_layer: Analytics 2 is a football-only add-on that tracks distance, speed, sprints, tackles, duels, dribbles, interceptions, passes and conversion rate per player and links jersey numbers to invited users [veo-17]. In Italy it costs 679 euros per year on Starter and Team, 799 on Club and 1,699 on Enterprise, while the older Analytics tier costs 259 to 799 euros per year [veo-02]. Player Spotlight, priced from 329 euros per year, produces individual highlight reels [veo-02].
criteria.integrations: The Veo Editor page names no third-party analysis integrations, and export is limited to MP4 follow-cam files and clips [veo-24, veo-23]. In Italy the analysis vendor Sics states that Veo footage is compatible with its VideoMatch software and presents itself as an official partner [veo-26]. Veo League Exchange gives leagues a shared video library, and the sub-processor list notes that exchange participants without a Veo subscription have their data stored in AWS us-east-1 [veo-25, veo-16].
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is limited to the Veo Live app for fans, RTMP output to YouTube, Facebook or another platform via the Live add-on, and shared links or clips [veo-04, veo-20]. There is no white-label OTT product, no pay-per-view and no advertising layer in the catalogue [veo-01, veo-02]. Federation deals such as US Youth Soccer and the LND are structured as member discounts and carry no distribution rights [veo-25, veo-11].
criteria.data_access_ownership: Customers can download the follow-cam view as MP4 on all plans above Starter, but the panoramic and interactive views, drawings and Analytics data cannot be downloaded [veo-23]. Storage is six months on Starter and Veo Go and twelve months on Team, Club and Enterprise, so long-term archives depend on the club exporting files itself [veo-04]. The data processing agreement obliges Veo to delete or return personal data at the controller's choice on termination [veo-17].
criteria.privacy_compliance: Veo positions itself as data processor and the club as controller, refers data-subject enquiries back to the club and publishes a GDPR Article 28 data processing agreement dated 18 August 2026 [veo-14, veo-17]. Recordings are stored in AWS eu-west-1 in Dublin, with EU-US transfers under the Data Privacy Framework and standard contractual clauses for other transfers [veo-16]. No face blurring, no opt-out for individuals on the pitch and no specific guidance on minors appear in the public documents [veo-14, veo-17].
criteria.security: Veo states that its data centres are ISO 27001 certified, that all traffic is encrypted over HTTPS and that it runs annual penetration tests, but it publishes no certification of its own [veo-15]. Infrastructure activity is logged through the cloud provider's native audit logging and the DPA grants the controller audit rights at its own expense [veo-17]. There is no public SOC 2 report or status page in the documents reviewed [veo-15].
criteria.pricing_tco: In Italy a football club pays 1,299 euros for the camera, 249 euros for the 5.2 metre tripod and 929 euros per year on the Team plan, which gives a first-year cost of roughly 2,477 euros before VAT and before add-ons [veo-02]. Multi-year terms cut the annual figure, with Team at 1,599 euros for 24 months and 2,099 euros for 36 months [veo-02]. Veo Go at 279 euros per year with free rig and tripod is the lowest entry price in this database for full-pitch stitched video, while the US market pays 999 dollars for Starter and 1,399 dollars for Team on the same plans [veo-02, veo-01].
criteria.support_service: Support runs through the help centre and a ticket system that requires an account, with priority support and a dedicated account manager reserved for Enterprise [veo-04, veo-20]. The repair policy gives one year of free repair or replacement for manufacturing defects and paid repair in years two and three, with no published turnaround time [veo-18]. Reviews split between customers praising fast responses and customers who escalated to the CEO to get a battery replaced [veo-21].
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Veo Technologies ApS reported revenue of 503.9 million Danish kroner in 2025, up from 446.1 million in 2024, with the annual loss narrowing from 58.1 million to 4.6 million kroner and equity of 177.9 million kroner [veo-08]. The company raised 80 million dollars in Series C in June 2022 led by pension fund ATP, employs around 320 people and counts Chr. Augustinus Fabrikker as a more than 10 percent shareholder [veo-09, veo-10]. Recent product direction is visible in the catalogue, with Analytics 2, Veo Go and School plans added and Cam 3 hardware unchanged since 2024 [veo-01, veo-02].
criteria.evidence_references: Italian customers shown on veo.com/it include Cittadella, Südtirol, AC Crema, Como and Ciliverghe Calcio, with a Primavera match analyst quoted [veo-13]. Federation partnerships include the Lega Nazionale Dilettanti, US Youth Soccer on a five-year term with a 200 dollar camera discount, and several English county FAs [veo-11, veo-25, veo-13]. The LND announcement carries Veo's own scale claims of 4.5 million matches recorded, 2.5 million registered users and activity in more than 100 countries [veo-11]. Italian trade press in August 2026 lists the Cam 3 among the reference cameras for football with the subscription dependency as its main drawback [veo-27].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: The Veo Cam app scores 4.7 from 1,500 ratings and the Veo Live app 4.8 from 13,000, while Trustpilot sits at 4.0 with 49 percent five-star and 34 percent one-star reviews [veo-19, veo-20, veo-21]. Coaches praise the reliability of the tracking and the ease of use, and complain about analytics gaps, the wide default framing and the cost of add-ons described as being nickel and dimed [veo-19, veo-21]. Support tickets left open for months appear in both app store and Trustpilot reviews [veo-19, veo-21].
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Veo Cam 3 records locally and all AI processing, stitching, follow-cam and event detection happen in Veo's AWS cloud after upload, so nothing is available until the file has been transferred and processed [veo-17, veo-06]. Live streaming is the exception, with the camera pushing a stream directly while recording [veo-07]. Veo Go processes nothing on the phone beyond capture and depends entirely on the upload of two files [veo-22].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The Editor and website are available in English, Italian, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Polish [veo-24]. Veo runs an Italian marketing team with a named Italy marketing manager quoted by the LND [veo-11]. Veo Go excludes iPhone SE and iPhone 16e, so the phone route depends on the handsets a team already owns [veo-22].
criteria.upgrade_path: A club can start on Veo Go at 279 euros per year, move to a Cam 3 with Starter or Team, and add Analytics 2, Live or Player Spotlight without changing platform [veo-02, veo-22]. Plans scale to Club at 10 teams and Enterprise at 20 teams, with catalogue discounts for upgrading from an Editor-only plan [veo-02]. There is no path to fixed multi-camera production or white-label OTT inside Veo [veo-04].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the follow-cam framing on a wide pitch against the interactive panorama, because reviewers say the automatic view stays wide [veo-19]. Test Analytics 2 jersey-number linking on a youth team with rotating shirts, since the whole individual data layer depends on it [veo-17]. Test the download workflow end to end, because only the follow-cam MP4 leaves the platform [veo-23].

free.one_line: zone14 rents Austrian built fixed 4K twin camera systems to football clubs on a subscription from EUR 115 to about EUR 130 a month, bundled with its REPLAY analysis software and optional video based player fitness data [zone14-01, zone14-02, zone14-03].
free.who_for: Amateur, semi professional and academy football clubs in German speaking Europe and Croatia that want every home match and training session recorded from a permanent mount and analysed by their own coaches [zone14-02, zone14-04]. It suits clubs that own or control their ground, since the cameras are mains powered and installed once [zone14-02].
free.why: zone14 exists because two Viennese founders saw that amateur clubs training four times a week wanted professional style video analysis and that no fixed camera came bundled with the software and the data to do it, so they built the camera, the analysis tool and a video based tracking layer as one subscription [zone14-05, zone14-02]. It matters now because the Bavarian football association made it official technology partner for more than 4,500 clubs and SK Rapid and Austria Wien's academy use it, which shows a European coaching first alternative to the broadcast and parent led models can reach scale [zone14-06, zone14-07]. It tells you that in Europe the buyer with the steadiest budget is still the club, and that a vendor that replaces GPS vests with video data has a second reason to be paid.
free.price_band: From EUR 115/month with camera and hardware included (company statement); CORE listed at EUR 130/month, EUR 1,560 billed yearly on the German page after a stated EUR 1,400 sponsorship; ELITE on request; REPLAY software only EUR 20/month

italy.note: zone14 lists Austria, Germany and Croatia as its markets with English, German and Croatian sites, and no Italian club, reseller or pricing was found [zone14-07, zone14-01].

verdict.look_if: You are a club in Austria, Germany or Croatia with your own pitch and coaches who will use tagging, drawing and playlists every week, and you want video based distance and sprint data without buying GPS vests [zone14-01, zone14-04]. You want a fixed system with lifetime hardware upgrades, unlimited downloads and 24/7 WhatsApp support for a monthly fee with no hardware purchase [zone14-01].
verdict.skip_if: You need a portable camera for away games and tournaments, since zone14 TWO is mounted permanently and mains powered [zone14-02, zone14-04]. You want live distribution to fans or a paywall, because livestreaming is a one click YouTube add on and there is no OTT or monetisation layer [zone14-01].
watch_outs: The English pricing page shows CORE and ELITE as price on request while the German page lists CORE at EUR 130 a month, EUR 1,560 billed yearly, described as including EUR 1,400 of sponsorship, so the unsubsidised list price is higher and must be confirmed in writing [zone14-01, zone14-03].
On the CORE tier recordings become available four hours after the final whistle and are capped at 70 recordings a year, with live availability and unlimited recordings reserved for ELITE [zone14-01].
4G connectivity costs extra or requires your own SIM, so a pitch without wired internet adds to the monthly bill [zone14-01].

zone14 counted over 65 clubs in five countries in May 2024 and over 200 installed systems in Europe by the BFV announcement, so it is a small company whose founders aimed to reach break even in 2025 [zone14-05, zone14-06].

The website privacy policy covers cookies and the site only, and no public document describes where match video is hosted or how long it is retained beyond the one year minimum [zone14-09, zone14-01].

criteria.use_case_fit: zone14 is a coaching first product for football clubs at every level, with SK Rapid using it on training pitches, FK Austria Wien's sports science team and regional league clubs such as Wiener Sport Club and SV Lafnitz as testimonials [zone14-01, zone14-02]. Training recording with multiple balls is supported on ELITE, which is unusual and useful for academies [zone14-01]. It is a match and training analysis tool with no fan facing layer.
criteria.capture_quality: zone14 TWO uses two 4K tracking cameras with integrated microphones to produce a 180 degree panoramic view of the pitch, mounted once and connected to mains power [zone14-04, zone14-01]. Frame rate, sensor and low light figures are not published, so ask for sample footage from an evening match under floodlights.
criteria.automation_accuracy: The AI follows play automatically so no camera operator is needed, and zone14 STATS derives per player tracking from the same video to produce distance, sprints and high intensity runs [zone14-04, zone14-01]. No independent accuracy benchmark exists for either the framing or the fitness data, and the fitness metrics should be validated against GPS on a few sessions before replacing vests.
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Two cameras are stitched into a single panoramic recording from which the tracked view is cut, and a Goal Cam add on is listed for ELITE [zone14-04, zone14-01]. There is no multi position camera coverage beyond that.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live features are add ons or ELITE inclusions: live tagging synced after the match, remote analysis during the game, second screen access to REPLAY, precision replay of each scene, half time analysis and one click YouTube livestreaming [zone14-01]. On CORE the recording is available four hours after the match [zone14-01]. Stream latency is not published.
criteria.reliability_resilience: The system is mains powered with no charging, installed once with no regular maintenance, uploads automatically after the final whistle and includes a camera status checker and lifetime hardware upgrades [zone14-01, zone14-04]. Recordings are stored for at least one year [zone14-01]. No public complaint history was found, and the customer base is small enough that none should be expected.
criteria.portability_install: Installation is a one time job of 20 to 40 minutes with a mounting plate, a few screws and a connection box, supported by zone14's team, and a suitability check for the venue is offered before ordering [zone14-01, zone14-04]. The camera does not travel, so away matches need a second solution.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Uploads run over 4G, WiFi or Ethernet, with 4G offered for an additional charge or through the club's own SIM [zone14-04, zone14-01]. Bandwidth requirements are not published.
criteria.workflow_ux: Matches are scheduled online by team, venue and time and the cameras record and upload without anyone present, then coaches work in REPLAY with drawing tools, saved drawings on the timeline, customisable and multiple tagging boards, cross match playlists, offline clips, playback speed control and user management [zone14-04, zone14-01]. Support runs through a WhatsApp group with the zone14 team on CORE and above [zone14-01].
criteria.analysis_layer: REPLAY is a full amateur analysis suite with unlimited tags and playlists, and STATS adds video derived fitness data with visualisations as an add on, included in ELITE [zone14-01]. A COACH product and an AI as a service offer are listed in the site navigation without public detail [zone14-01]. This is the deepest analysis layer among the five vendors in this batch.
criteria.integrations: Third party footage can be uploaded to REPLAY on the EUR 20 tier or as an add on, and livestreams go to YouTube [zone14-01]. No API, federation database link or export to other analysis platforms is documented.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is limited to one click YouTube livestreaming as an add on and clip downloads for social media [zone14-01]. There is no white label platform, paywall or advertising layer.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Full match downloads and clip downloads are unlimited on the camera tiers and recordings are kept for a minimum of one year [zone14-01]. Terms on ownership after cancellation and on hosting location are not published [zone14-09].
criteria.privacy_compliance: zone14 GmbH is an Austrian company subject to GDPR and its imprint lists the register number and managing directors [zone14-10]. The public privacy policy addresses the website only and no blurring, opt out or minors policy is documented for match footage, so clubs filming youth teams need their own consent process [zone14-09]. Footage stays within the club's REPLAY account and never reaches a public platform, which limits exposure compared with broadcast models [zone14-01].
criteria.pricing_tco: zone14 states the system starts at EUR 115 a month including the camera and all hardware, the German page lists CORE at EUR 130 a month or EUR 1,560 a year after a stated EUR 1,400 sponsorship, REPLAY software alone costs EUR 20 a month and ELITE is on request [zone14-03, zone14-01].
