free.name: BallerCam (Baller, Inc. / BallerTV)
free.payer_model_label: Family or coach buys the device
free.one_line: BallerCam is a $299 shell with a 180-degree lens, cooling fan and battery that turns an iPhone 13 Pro or newer into an AI camera that records, livestreams and clips youth basketball, soccer, futsal and volleyball games [ballercam-01, ballercam-02].
free.who_for: US and Canadian parents, team managers and club coaches who already own a recent iPhone and want automated filming and free livestreaming without a per-viewer or per-team subscription [ballercam-01, ballercam-08]. It is a family product first, and coaches use it because the footage and clips come free of per-seat fees [ballercam-06].
free.why: BallerTV built BallerCam because eight years of streaming more than two million youth games with paid crews and fixed cameras taught it that the unit economics only work if the family owns the capture device, so it packaged its computer vision into a phone shell and launched it in July 2025 with Alex Morgan as investor and face [ballercam-03, ballercam-04]. It matters now because a $299 one-off device with a free 20-hour cloud tier undercuts every fixed camera with a mandatory subscription and pushes the category toward hardware-light, app-heavy products [ballercam-02, ballercam-05]. It tells you the youth capture market is splitting into two, a club tier that buys a dedicated camera and a family tier that buys an accessory for the phone it already carries, and that the second tier will be won on app reliability and storage economics [ballercam-06, ballercam-07].
free.price_band: $299 one-off device (list $349); cloud storage free for 20 hours, $99/yr for 100 hours, $199/yr for 250 hours

italy.note: New devices ship only to the US and Canada, the app works anywhere with an iPhone and connectivity, and the terms state the service is intended for users in the United States [ballercam-08, ballercam-11].

free.evidence_note: Device price, plan prices, plan contents, shipping scope, terms and privacy policy verified from Baller, Inc. pages and the App Store listing; review sentiment from App Store reviews; company funding history from PitchBook.

verdict.look_if: You are a US or Canadian parent, team manager or small-club coach with an iPhone 13 Pro or newer and you want automated filming plus free livestreaming to family for a one-off $299 [ballercam-01, ballercam-08]. You should also look if you coach basketball, where the live scoring, clip creation and January 2026 advanced stats features are most developed [ballercam-05, ballercam-13].
verdict.skip_if: You are in Europe, since Baller only ships new devices to the US and Canada and its terms and privacy policy are written for US users with no GDPR section [ballercam-08, ballercam-10, ballercam-11]. You should also skip it if you need a full-pitch football recording tall enough for tactical analysis, since the camera sits on an 80-inch tripod and reviewers report tracking loss at greater heights [ballercam-06, ballercam-07].
watch_outs: The terms of service grant Baller, Inc. a perpetual, irrevocable, transferable, worldwide licence to use, modify, distribute and exploit user recordings without compensation, which is broader than most camera vendors [ballercam-11].
The privacy policy states the service is not directed to children under 13 and contains no GDPR or EU rights section, so an EU club would carry the compliance work itself [ballercam-10].

The App Store shows 4.9 stars from 505 ratings, and the critical reviews describe app freezes at setup, storage errors that block livestreams, misaligned clip markers across multiple devices and uploads taking one to two hours per game [ballercam-06, ballercam-07].
Baller recommends 10 GB of free iPhone storage per hour of filming and a 5 Mbps upload for streaming, so a two-game day needs a phone with real headroom [ballercam-09].
Filming is iPhone-only, iPhone 13 Pro or newer, with no Android filming app [ballercam-09].
BallerTV's last disclosed venture round dates from September 2021, and no 2025 or 2026 financing has been announced beyond Alex Morgan's strategic investment [ballercam-04, ballercam-14].

criteria.use_case_fit: BallerCam targets family and team filming of youth basketball, volleyball, soccer and futsal, with American football, flag football and 7v7 supported through a dedicated guide and lacrosse and hockey listed as under consideration [ballercam-01, ballercam-05, ballercam-12]. The design centre is indoor court sports at 80-inch tripod height, which fits basketball well and full-size football pitches less well [ballercam-01, ballercam-07]. Coaches get scoring, roster and clip tools, and the January 2026 advanced stats release added player-attributed rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and fouls for basketball [ballercam-13].
criteria.capture_quality: The device records 4K on the phone with 1080p downloads, and the livestream runs at 720p and auto-adjusts to connection speed [ballercam-01]. The optical path is a patent-pending ultra-wide lens giving a 180-degree sideline view, from which the app crops, pans and zooms in real time on the phone [ballercam-03, ballercam-04]. Reviewers describe clear video and good audio, and one review notes the desktop 180-degree viewer allows a coach to pick any angle after the game [ballercam-06].
criteria.automation_accuracy: Tracking runs on-device with computer vision trained on BallerTV's archive of more than two million games [ballercam-04]. Positive reviews say the ball tracking does very well for basketball, while a two-star review reports the tracker losing the ball when the camera is mounted above the 80-inch tripod height [ballercam-06, ballercam-07]. Auto highlights are still listed as coming soon on the pricing page, and the current clip workflow relies on a scorer logging plays that the app then clips automatically [ballercam-05, ballercam-13].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: BallerCam is a single-lens, single-phone product with no multi-camera stitching [ballercam-01]. Multiple phones can join a game for scoring and moment marking, and reviewers report time-sync drift between devices that misaligns moment markers [ballercam-07]. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Livestreaming is included on every plan at 720p with adaptive bitrate, viewers watch in a browser without an account, and the Pro plan adds RTMP out and a custom video logo [ballercam-05, ballercam-12]. Baller recommends a 5 Mbps upload and reviewers say a full signal is needed for a stable stream [ballercam-07, ballercam-09]. Latency figures are not published.
criteria.reliability_resilience: The shell has a cooling fan powered by the swappable battery pack and ships with a sun shade, which Baller recommends for heat protection [ballercam-01, ballercam-09]. The app can record locally without internet and upload later [ballercam-09]. The reliability complaints in the App Store concern the software, with freezes at setup, storage errors and disappearing uploads reported by two-star reviewers against a 4.9 average from 505 ratings [ballercam-06, ballercam-07].
criteria.portability_install: The kit is a shell, phone adapter, battery, sun shade, back cover, cables and a sling bag, with an 80-inch ultra-portable tripod and a 15-foot outdoor tripod sold as accessories [ballercam-01, ballercam-02]. Setup is described by reviewers as very easy, and positioning guidance is mid-court or mid-field [ballercam-06, ballercam-12]. The phone adapter is model-specific and one is included per purchase [ballercam-01].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Streaming needs a phone data or Wi-Fi connection of at least 5 Mbps upload, and record-only mode works offline [ballercam-09]. Reviewers report roughly 8 GB of footage per game and uploads that take one to two hours on ordinary connections [ballercam-07]. Baller's own guidance is 10 GB of free phone storage per hour filmed [ballercam-09].
criteria.workflow_ux: The filmer taps record or go live in the app, shares a private link, and family watch in a browser with no login [ballercam-12]. A scorer on a second device or an Apple Watch logs points and events that become clips and a live scoreboard [ballercam-05, ballercam-07]. Downloads at 1080p are available in-app immediately for the creator and on desktop after cloud upload, and team members get 720p immediately and 1080p after upload [ballercam-15]. The September 2026 app update added AI Plays feedback, live previews on the home screen and RSVP controls, which shows the roadmap is moving toward team management [ballercam-06].
criteria.analysis_layer: Analysis is limited to scoring, play tagging, player attribution and a Game Breakdown view for basketball introduced in January 2026, with manual stat editing promised for spring 2026 [ballercam-12, ballercam-13]. There is no tactical drawing, no automatic event detection for football and no export to third-party analysis platforms documented [ballercam-05]. Auto-generated highlight reels remain on the roadmap [ballercam-13].
criteria.integrations: The Pro plan's RTMP output is the only documented integration and lets a club push the feed to YouTube or another platform [ballercam-05]. Footage can be stored on the phone, in BallerCam cloud or exported to third-party storage [ballercam-12]. No documented integrations with league platforms, analysis software or club management tools were found.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is BallerCam's own browser viewer with private links and no viewer accounts, backed by the BallerTV platform heritage [ballercam-04, ballercam-12]. There is no paywall or pay-per-view for viewers, so the model is free sharing to family and friends [ballercam-05]. Pro-plan RTMP allows onward distribution to a third-party OTT service [ballercam-05].
criteria.data_access_ownership: Users keep copyright in their recordings, but the terms grant Baller, Inc. a perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, transferable, worldwide licence to host, modify, distribute and exploit user content without compensation, plus rights to use names, images and likenesses in promotion [ballercam-11]. The FAQ states Baller never sells user data or shares recordings without explicit permission, and users can manage, download or delete saved games at any time [ballercam-05, ballercam-12]. Stored hours beyond the plan allowance are governed by a fair use policy that is referenced but not published in detail [ballercam-05].
criteria.privacy_compliance: The privacy policy names Baller, Inc. at 844 E Green St, Pasadena, collects contact, profile, athletic statistics, audio-visual content and information about non-users appearing in uploaded video, and includes a US state consumer privacy supplement with no GDPR section [ballercam-10]. The service is described as a general audience service not directed to children under 13, and the terms say it is intended for users in the United States [ballercam-10, ballercam-11]. The App Store privacy label lists contact info, user IDs and usage data linked to identity and precise location unlinked [ballercam-06]. Facial recognition and biometric processing are not mentioned in the policy [ballercam-10].
criteria.security: Livestreams and replays are shared through private links and viewers do not need accounts [ballercam-12]. The privacy policy states payments are processed by third parties and that data may be transferred from the US to other countries for storage and processing [ballercam-10]. No security certification, encryption statement or penetration testing disclosure was found.
criteria.pricing_tco: The device costs $299, reduced from $349, with a 30-day return window and a one-year warranty [ballercam-01, ballercam-02]. Cloud storage is free for 20 hours, then $99 per year for 100 hours or $199 per year for 250 hours, with unlimited filming hours on all plans subject to fair use [ballercam-02]. The Club Basketball Bundle adds the 80-inch tripod at the same $299 [ballercam-16]. Subscriptions auto-renew annually with no prorated refunds [ballercam-11]. A typical family therefore pays $299 once and nothing more if they delete or download games, while a club team filming forty games a year pays $299 plus $99 to $199 per year, which is a fraction of any fixed-camera subscription [ballercam-02].
criteria.support_service: Support runs through a Zendesk help centre with more than 76 articles and a request form, and the App Store page shows support responding to reviews and resolving glitches [ballercam-06, ballercam-09]. Shipping is same day before 2 PM Eastern on weekdays, free within the continental US, with prepaid return labels for devices [ballercam-01, ballercam-17]. No SLA or phone support is published.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Baller, Inc. trades as BallerTV, was founded in 2016 in Pasadena, and PitchBook records $64.4 million raised with the last round a Series B in September 2021 from investors including Bessemer Venture Partners, plus acquisitions of FieldVision in 2019 and NextPro in 2021 [ballercam-04, ballercam-14]. Alex Morgan joined as strategic investor and brand ambassador at the July 2025 launch [ballercam-03]. The roadmap published in January 2026 names autogenerated highlight reels, deeper stats and athlete profiles, and the September 2026 app release shipped AI Plays feedback and team RSVP tools [ballercam-06, ballercam-13]. Revenue and profitability are not public.
criteria.evidence_references: The strongest evidence is Baller's own product, pricing, terms, privacy and support pages, the PR Newswire launch release and the App Store listing with 505 ratings [ballercam-01, ballercam-02, ballercam-03, ballercam-06, ballercam-10, ballercam-11]. Third-party evidence is limited to PitchBook's funding summary and Prep Network coverage of the launch [ballercam-14, ballercam-18]. No independent lab test or European review was found.
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Five-star reviews praise setup ease, clear video, the desktop angle picker for teaching and the absence of per-person fees, and a coach review says the ball is tracked well in basketball [ballercam-06]. Two-star reviews cite bugs, multi-device sync drift, clip playback showing the wrong segment and slow uploads [ballercam-07]. The pattern is a happy family user base and a more frustrated power user base that runs several devices per game [ballercam-06, ballercam-07].
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Tracking, cropping and encoding happen on the iPhone using on-device computer vision, and the cloud handles storage, viewing and the 180-degree interactive viewer [ballercam-03, ballercam-05]. The phone-side load explains the cooling fan, the 10 GB per hour storage guidance and the need for a Pro-class iPhone [ballercam-01, ballercam-09]. Record-only sessions work without connectivity and upload later [ballercam-09].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The app is English only, requires iOS 17 or later and supports an Apple Watch companion for scoring [ballercam-06]. Viewers watch in any desktop or mobile browser without an account [ballercam-12]. No localisation for European markets is published.
criteria.upgrade_path: The upgrade path is software, since the same shell gains features through app updates, with new model-specific iPhone adapters sold separately as phones change [ballercam-01, ballercam-02]. Plan upgrades move from free to $99 and $199 storage tiers and unlock RTMP and custom logos at Pro [ballercam-05]. There is no documented path into BallerTV's paid event streaming or into any analysis platform.
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the 180-degree interactive viewer on desktop, since the ability to pick any angle after the game is the feature coaches single out [ballercam-06]. Test livestream stability on a venue Wi-Fi at 5 Mbps and measure upload time for a full game, since these are the two recurring complaints [ballercam-07, ballercam-09]. Test tracking on a full-size football pitch from the 15-foot outdoor tripod to see whether the basketball-first tracker holds up outdoors [ballercam-02, ballercam-07].

free.name: FoloCam (FoloCam LLC)
free.payer_model_label: Family or coach buys the device
free.one_line: FoloCam is an iOS app that pairs an iPhone 13 or newer with an Apple DockKit motorised gimbal and uses on-device AI to keep the ball in frame for soccer and basketball, recording 4K locally for $49.99 a year [folocam-01, folocam-02].
free.who_for: Parents and volunteer coaches who already own a recent iPhone and want a full-match recording that follows the ball for the price of a cheap gimbal and a low subscription, with no cloud account and no hardware lock-in [folocam-01, folocam-03]. It suits people who are comfortable with a one-developer product and will handle their own storage and sharing [folocam-03].
free.why: FoloCam exists because Apple's DockKit framework and the Neural Engine in recent iPhones made it possible for a single developer, Gilbert Chen of Duplicacy and ActionStitch, to ship a ball-tracking camera as a $49.99 app, where the incumbents ship a $1,000 device [folocam-03, folocam-05]. It matters now because it sets the floor price for automated football filming at roughly $100 of gimbal plus $50 a year, with all processing on the phone and no video leaving the device, which is a privacy posture the cloud-based incumbents cannot match [folocam-02, folocam-04]. It tells you the capture layer is commoditising fast, that the value is moving to the platform and analysis layers, and that solo and small developers can now attack the low end of the market from the App Store [folocam-05, folocam-06].
free.price_band: App free for 10-minute recordings; $49.99/yr (€59.99/yr in Italy) for unlimited recording and RTMP; $150 Amazon kit with gimbal and lifetime subscription; DockKit gimbal from about $35 to $100 extra

italy.note: The app is listed on the Italian App Store with the Premium Yearly in-app purchase at €59.99, and the gimbals it supports are sold through ordinary consumer retail [folocam-07].

free.evidence_note: Pricing, compatibility, on-device processing and privacy claims verified from FoloCam's site, support page, App Store listings in the US and Italy and the developer's forums; company scale and sentiment from the developer's own statements and a small user forum, with no third-party review found.

watch_outs: FoloCam is a one-person company, the developer states there are no investors and no plans to be acquired, and the roadmap depends on one person's time [folocam-03].

The lifetime subscription in the $150 Amazon kit is tied to the gimbal, so a broken or replaced gimbal raises the question of what happens to the licence [folocam-08, folocam-09].

Users on the developer's forum report video freezes and slow tracking, gimbal motor noise and a loss of ball sight a couple of times per match in sample footage, and 4K60 is flagged by the developer as experimental and likely to slow tracking [folocam-10, folocam-11, folocam-12].
DockKit gimbals need NFC pairing before the app can drive them, and the DJI Osmo Mobile 8P remote cannot be used at the same time as FoloCam [folocam-12].
The current App Store build requires iOS 26 or later, which excludes older phones even where the site says iPhone 13 or newer [folocam-06].

criteria.use_case_fit: FoloCam is built for soccer and basketball, with more sports listed as coming soon and hockey mentioned by forum users [folocam-01, folocam-11]. It fits parents and volunteer coaches who want a single wide-to-medium recording that follows the ball, with no broadcast-style production, and the developer positions it against Veo and XbotGo on price [folocam-05]. It is a recording tool with no viewer product, so it is a poor fit for clubs that need to distribute matches to families [folocam-02].
criteria.capture_quality: Recording is 4K30 on the iPhone camera at 2x zoom, with 4K60 experimental since version 1.4 in May 2026 [folocam-02, folocam-10]. The developer recommends iPhone 15 or newer for lossless 2x zoom on a full pitch, and a Soccer Pro mode is limited to iPhone 14 Pro, 15, 16 and 17 class devices [folocam-02]. Image quality is therefore the phone's own, which on a current iPhone exceeds most dedicated youth cameras in resolution, and the field of view is a single moving frame with no panoramic stitch [folocam-01].
criteria.automation_accuracy: Tracking runs on the iPhone Neural Engine and the developer claims it can spot the ball near the far corner of a full field and follow it for most of a full-field match [folocam-01, folocam-05]. A forum user watching the developer's sample noted the system loses sight of the ball a couple of times, and another thread reports video freezes and slow tracking, so real-world consistency is still being tuned through frequent releases [folocam-09, folocam-11]. Basketball got a Pro mode and faster pan speed in versions 1.4 and 1.5 [folocam-06, folocam-10].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: FoloCam drives one phone on one gimbal and produces a single recording with no multi-camera stitching [folocam-01]. The developer's separate ActionStitch product stitches two action cameras into a 180-degree panorama, which shows the capability exists in the same hands but is not part of FoloCam [folocam-03].
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live output is an RTMP push to a server URL and stream key, available only with the paid subscription [folocam-02]. There is no built-in viewer page, no adaptive bitrate statement and no published latency, so live readiness depends entirely on the destination platform and the venue's upload bandwidth [folocam-02].
criteria.reliability_resilience: All processing is local, so the recording continues without connectivity, and the app now warns on low storage [folocam-02, folocam-06]. Reliability issues reported by users are gimbal disconnections before NFC pairing, motor noise and occasional freezes in tracking [folocam-11, folocam-12]. Heat and battery behaviour over a 90-minute match at 4K with continuous inference is not documented and depends on the phone [folocam-02].
criteria.portability_install: The whole kit is a phone, a pocket gimbal and a tripod, which is the most portable setup in the category [folocam-01]. Setup requires NFC pairing of the DockKit gimbal, then mounting at a sideline position, and the developer recommends the cheaper Comitok Mogo over premium gimbals for this use [folocam-12]. Height and position guidance is limited to forum advice [folocam-11].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: No connectivity is needed to record, since tracking and video processing run on the phone and nothing is uploaded to FoloCam servers [folocam-02]. RTMP streaming needs whatever upload bandwidth the chosen bitrate demands, and no figures are published [folocam-02]. Files are stored in the iOS Files app under a FoloCam folder [folocam-02].
criteria.workflow_ux: The user pairs the gimbal, opens the app, chooses the sport and mode, and presses record, and the video lands in the Files app for manual sharing [folocam-02]. There is no cloud library, no team roster, no highlights and no clip tool, and users are asking on the forum for Apple Watch remote control, external microphone support and a live score overlay [folocam-11]. Version 1.5 added a watermark removal option [folocam-06].
criteria.analysis_layer: There is no analysis layer, no tagging and no statistics [folocam-02]. Users can take the recorded file into any third-party analysis tool by hand [folocam-02].
criteria.integrations: The only integration is a generic RTMP output for paid users [folocam-02]. Hardware integration is through Apple DockKit with the Insta360 Flow Pro, Flow 2 Pro, DJI Osmo Mobile 8 and Comitok Mogo listed as compatible, and the DJI Osmo Mobile 8P works after NFC pairing with the caveat that its remote cannot run at the same time [folocam-02, folocam-12].
criteria.distribution_ott: FoloCam has no distribution product, so families watch either through a third-party RTMP destination such as YouTube or through files shared manually after the match [folocam-02]. This keeps it firmly in the capture layer.
criteria.data_access_ownership: The user holds the only copy of the recording on their phone, since nothing is uploaded to FoloCam servers and the app collects no personal data [folocam-02, folocam-06]. There is no vendor licence over footage because the vendor never receives it [folocam-02]. Export is a plain file in the Files app [folocam-02].
criteria.privacy_compliance: The App Store privacy label states the developer does not collect any data from this app, and the support page says FoloCam collects no personal data and that all ball tracking and video processing runs on the iPhone [folocam-02, folocam-06]. For an EU club this removes the processor relationship entirely, leaving only the club's own obligations around filming minors [folocam-02]. No published GDPR statement, DPA or children's policy exists because none is needed for the app itself, though the RTMP destination will carry its own terms [folocam-02].
criteria.security: Recordings stay on the device and no account is created, which reduces the attack surface to the phone itself [folocam-02]. No security documentation is published. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.pricing_tco: The app is free for unlimited 10-minute recordings, $49.99 per year in the US and €59.99 per year in Italy for unlimited duration and RTMP, and there is no monthly plan [folocam-02, folocam-06, folocam-07, folocam-13]. The $150 Amazon kit bundles a gimbal with a lifetime subscription tied to that gimbal, and the developer has offered promo codes bringing a compatible gimbal to $35 [folocam-05, folocam-08]. A three-year total for a family is therefore about $100 for a gimbal plus $150 of subscription, or $150 once with the kit, against $1,000 and more for a dedicated camera with mandatory subscription [folocam-02, folocam-08].
criteria.support_service: Support is the developer answering on the FoloCam user community forum and the ActionStitch forum, and the about page states he personally replies to almost every question [folocam-03, folocam-11]. Threads from September 2026 show replies within a day [folocam-12]. There is no phone support, SLA or reseller network.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: FoloCam LLC is an independent US company run solely by Gilbert Chen, who states there are no investors, no growth headcount and no plans to be acquired, and that the roadmap follows user requests and Apple silicon capabilities [folocam-03]. The app launched in March 2026 and has shipped versions 1.3, 1.4 and 1.5 between then and June 2026, adding Basketball Pro, 4K60 and watermark removal [folocam-05, folocam-06, folocam-10]. Financials are not public and the company's continuity rests on one person [folocam-03].
criteria.evidence_references: Primary evidence comes from the FoloCam site, support page, about page and App Store listings in the US and Italy [folocam-01, folocam-02, folocam-03, folocam-06, folocam-07]. User sentiment comes from the developer-run forums, where the developer moderates, and from the ActionStitch forum announcements [folocam-05, folocam-09, folocam-11]. No independent review or test was found, and the Junior Grassroots Hub partner page referenced in search results returned a 404 [folocam-14].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Forum users are enthusiastic about price and simplicity and are actively requesting features such as motion profiles, individual player tracking, higher frame rates and live scores, which signals a small base of engaged early adopters [folocam-11]. Complaints concentrate on tracking freezes, gimbal noise and DJI compatibility [folocam-11, folocam-12]. There are two US App Store ratings, both five stars [folocam-06].
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: FoloCam is entirely edge, with detection, gimbal control and encoding on the iPhone and no cloud component at all [folocam-02]. The trade-off is that features which need heavy compute, such as multi-angle stitching or event detection, are constrained by the phone and the developer flags 4K60 as slowing tracking [folocam-10].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The app is in English and Simplified Chinese, requires iOS 26 or later, and is distributed through App Stores worldwide including Italy [folocam-06, folocam-07]. There is no Android version and users have asked for one [folocam-11].
criteria.upgrade_path: Upgrades arrive as app releases and as new iPhones, since tracking quality scales with the phone's Neural Engine, and the developer explicitly ties the roadmap to Apple silicon [folocam-03]. There is no path into a platform or analysis product from the same vendor, so a club that outgrows it changes vendor [folocam-02].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test full-pitch tracking on an 11-a-side game from the halfway line with an iPhone 15 or newer at 2x, since that is the developer's headline claim [folocam-01, folocam-02]. Test a 90-minute recording for heat throttling and battery on the phone model your coaches carry, since no vendor data exists [folocam-02]. Test the Comitok Mogo against the Insta360 Flow Pro for motor noise and pan speed on basketball, where users report differences [folocam-11, folocam-12].

free.name: MOVE 'N SEE PIX4TEAM 2
free.payer_model_label: Family or coach buys the device
free.one_line: A French robotic pan-tilt head with a built-in 180-degree AI spotter camera that physically points your own camcorder or phone at the action, records to a microSD card and streams to YouTube or RTMP with no mandatory subscription.
free.who_for: Clubs, schools and parents who want a real optical zoom on a single team-sport pitch, own or will buy a camcorder, and prefer a one-off purchase to a cloud subscription. It suits people who accept a mechanical head and a tall stand in exchange for close-up broadcast framing with real optical zoom.
free.why: PIX4TEAM exists because Move'N See, a Brest company that started with beacon-tracked robotic cameras for equestrian riders, moved to a beacon-free AI spotter in 2019 so that team sports could get a real zoom lens following play without a camera operator [pix4team-01, pix4team-05]. It matters now because the company entered judicial reorganisation in January 2026 after a cessation of payments dated 31 December 2025, and the observation period runs to January 2027, which puts the two-year warranty, spare parts and firmware support of a hardware product in question [pix4team-05, pix4team-06]. It tells you that a hardware-only, subscription-free model is hard to sustain against cloud-funded competitors, even when the product is well engineered and priced below them.

verdict.look_if: You want optical zoom footage of one pitch, already own a compatible Sony, Canon or Panasonic camcorder or a recent phone, and you would rather pay once and keep the files on a microSD card than commit to a cloud subscription. Look also if you film indoor sports or equestrian events where a panoramic crop struggles and a pointed lens shines.
verdict.skip_if: You need a vendor that will be trading in two years, because Move'N See is in redressement judiciaire with an observation period running to January 2027. Skip also if you want automatic highlights, tagging, tactical panoramas or a fan platform, since PIX4TEAM records a single broadcast-style file and leaves everything else to optional services or third-party software.
watch_outs: MOVE'N SEE SAS entered redressement judiciaire at the Brest commercial court on 27 January 2026 with cessation of payments dated 31 December 2025, and the observation period was extended to 27 January 2027 on 21 July 2026 [pix4team-05, pix4team-06].

The €1,299 ex VAT price is a back-to-sports sale price against a €1,599 list price, advertised as valid through 15 September and still displayed on 19 September 2026, so the effective price could revert [pix4team-01].
The robot ships without a camera, stand or microSD card, so a working outdoor kit is the €2,479 ex VAT outdoor pack or the robot plus a €625 camcorder and a €319 to €469 heavy stand [pix4team-01].

The PIX4TEAM Remote app holds 3.2 stars from 21 Google Play reviews, with reports of repeated connection attempts, a tutorial overlay blocking Samsung navigation buttons and HDMI monitoring failures with some cameras [pix4team-07].
Battery life is 2.5 to 3.5 hours per NP-F970 pack, enough for one match with warm-up and little margin for a double header without a spare at €49 ex VAT [pix4team-01].
The minimum installation height is 4.8 metres and the head weighs 1.4 kg plus the camera, so a heavy stand, wind bracing and sandbags are needed outdoors, all sold separately [pix4team-01].
There is no panoramic recording, so a missed pan is footage lost for good [pix4team-01].

criteria.use_case_fit: PIX4TEAM 2 is a motorised head for team sports on pitches up to 100 by 100 metres, with dedicated AI per sport for football, basketball, rugby, hockey, handball and others, and it suits clubs that want one operator-free camera per pitch producing a single zoomed video [pix4team-01]. It also serves equestrian, which is where most of the reseller network sits [pix4team-03]. It does not produce a tactical wide view, data or highlights, so analysts who want a panorama should look elsewhere.
criteria.capture_quality: Image quality comes from whichever camera you mount, up to 1.5 kg, with automatic zoom control for more than 100 Sony and Canon models and a Panasonic HC-VX3 4K camcorder sold in the bundles, while phones and tablets under 11 inches work through the free PIX4TEAM Camera app [pix4team-01]. Because the lens physically follows play, the result is a true optical zoom broadcast-style frame with none of the softness of a digital crop from a panorama. Output resolution and bitrate are therefore the camera's, not the robot's.
criteria.automation_accuracy: A 5.1 MP 1/2.5-inch 180-degree spotter camera in the base films the whole field, an AI model decides where the action is, and the head pans at up to 120 degrees per second and tilts at 40 degrees per second to follow it without beacons or manual control [pix4team-01]. No accuracy figures are published, and one Google Play reviewer describes the head as overly reactive when the ball goes out of bounds [pix4team-07]. The sport-specific models and the 3 to 20 metre optimal distance from the field are the main tuning levers [pix4team-01].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: PIX4TEAM records a single moving frame from one camera and has no stitching, panorama or multi-camera production [pix4team-01]. A club wanting a second angle runs a second robot independently. Not applicable beyond that.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Live streaming to YouTube, Facebook, Twitch or any RTMP endpoint is free and unlimited, using a phone hotspot, WiFi or the Ethernet port on the head, and the optional MyTvChannel service adds sponsor overlays, a scoreboard and monetisation from €39 a month [pix4team-01, pix4team-02]. No latency figure is published. Streaming is a first-class feature.
criteria.reliability_resilience: The head records locally to microSD, runs 2.5 to 3.5 hours on the supplied NP-F970 battery or indefinitely on 19V mains, carries a two-year international warranty and is described as fully repairable after warranty, with a Move'N See Care damage plan at €9.50 a month [pix4team-01]. App reviews report connection retries and UI bugs after updates, and the Remote app was last updated on 15 September 2026, so development continues through the insolvency procedure [pix4team-07]. The bigger reliability risk is corporate.
criteria.portability_install: The head weighs 1.4 kg and measures 26 by 13 by 13 cm, mounts on a quarter-inch plate, and needs a minimum height of 4.8 metres, met by the 4.8-metre heavy stand at €319 or the 7.3-metre stand with wind bracing at €469, plus sandbags and a €129 rain cape outdoors [pix4team-01]. A transport bag costs €179. Setup is a carry-and-erect job for one person with a tall stand, heavier than a panoramic camera on a light tripod.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Recording needs no connection at all, control runs over WiFi from the PIX4TEAM Remote app, and streaming uses a phone hotspot, local WiFi or the Ethernet cable supplied in the box [pix4team-01]. No minimum upload speed is published. The design tolerates grounds with no internet.
criteria.workflow_ux: The free PIX4TEAM Remote app handles setup, field dimensions, recording and streaming, and the free PIX4TEAM Camera app turns a phone into the mounted camera with automatic zoom [pix4team-01]. Users ask for field dimensions to be remembered between sessions and report a tutorial overlay blocking navigation buttons on Samsung devices after a 2026 update [pix4team-07]. Files come off the microSD card as standard video for any editing or analysis tool.
criteria.analysis_layer: There is no analysis in the robot; Move'N See offers a separate video analysis and tagging platform from €19 a month for clipping, secure storage and sharing with teams, leagues, parents or referees [pix4team-02]. No tracking data, event data or automatic highlights are produced. Clubs using Hudl, Nacsport or Once Sport Analyser simply import the file.
criteria.integrations: Camera control covers more than 100 Sony and Canon models by cable and phones through the app, streaming targets any RTMP service, and a fixed-camera variant can be linked to a league score server according to the shop navigation [pix4team-01, pix4team-02]. No API or analysis platform integration is documented. Integration is at the file and RTMP level.
criteria.distribution_ott: Free unlimited streaming to YouTube, Facebook, Twitch and RTMP is built in, and MyTvChannel from €39 a month provides a dedicated amateur sports channel with sponsor banners and monetisation as an alternative to social platforms [pix4team-01, pix4team-02]. There is no pay-per-view mechanism described for the base product. For most clubs YouTube will be the distribution layer.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Footage is recorded to the club's own microSD card and never touches a vendor cloud unless the club chooses streaming or the optional storage platform, which is the simplest ownership position in this database [pix4team-01]. Terms for the optional platform are not detailed on the services page [pix4team-02]. Cloud retention is a question only for subscribers.
criteria.privacy_compliance: Local recording and no mandatory cloud mean that personal data processing stays with the club, and the spotter camera's image is used for tracking on the device [pix4team-01]. No consent guidance, blurring or minors policy is published. The vendor's own privacy policy covers the shop and apps only.
criteria.security: Not assessable from public sources. The shop is hosted on Amazon Web Services and no security documentation exists for the apps or optional services [pix4team-04].
criteria.pricing_tco: Robot €1,299 ex VAT on sale against €1,599 list, bundles at €1,955 with the Panasonic HC-VX3, €2,075 for the bleachers pack, €2,329 indoor and €2,479 outdoor, all ex VAT with inclusive prices shown at 20% French VAT [pix4team-01]. Recurring costs are optional: Care at €9.50, analysis platform from €19 and MyTvChannel from €39 a month, plus consumables such as a €49 spare battery [pix4team-01, pix4team-02]. Over three years a subscription-free outdoor kit costs about €2,500 ex VAT, which undercuts every camera-plus-cloud competitor, with the caveat that warranty service depends on the company surviving reorganisation [pix4team-05].
criteria.support_service: Support is advertised as fast, with a two-year international warranty, a 30-day money-back guarantee excluding shipping, repairability beyond warranty and developer replies on app store reviews pointing to firmware updates and direct contact [pix4team-01, pix4team-07]. The company has 10 to 19 employees and is operating under a court-supervised observation period, so response capacity should be checked before purchase [pix4team-06].
criteria.company_health_roadmap: MOVE'N SEE SAS, SIREN 531299246, founded in 2011 in Brest with capital of €184,433 and president Eric Willemenot de Nanc, has been in redressement judiciaire since 27 January 2026 with the observation period extended to 27 January 2027 and is noted as in default of publishing accounts [pix4team-05, pix4team-06, pix4team-04]. Product development continues, with app updates in September 2026 and an active sale campaign, and the outcome of the procedure, whether a continuation plan or a sale of the business, is unknown [pix4team-07, pix4team-01]. Buyers should treat the two-year warranty as uncertain.
criteria.evidence_references: The shop cites testimonial videos and no named clubs, and the reseller network spans about 20 countries with a heavy equestrian weighting, including B&H in New York, SolidSport in Stockholm and Scout10 in Spain [pix4team-08, pix4team-03]. The PIX4TEAM Remote app shows more than 5,000 installs on Google Play [pix4team-07]. No federation or league deployment is documented.
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Google Play users rate the Remote app 3.2 from 21 reviews, praising that the system works well overall while complaining about connection reliability, overlay bugs and jumpy tracking at out-of-bounds moments [pix4team-07]. No coach or analyst reviews of the footage itself are public. Sentiment is mixed on the app and unknown on the video.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Everything happens on the device: spotting, tracking, camera control and recording, with the cloud used only for optional streaming and services [pix4team-01, pix4team-02]. There is no processing delay after the match because the file is final when recording stops. This is the purest edge product in the database.
criteria.accessibility_languages: The shop and apps operate in English, French, Spanish and German, with a currency selector covering EUR, USD, GBP, CAD and AUD, and resellers cover most of Europe, North America, Australia and South Africa [pix4team-08, pix4team-01, pix4team-03]. No Italian interface or reseller exists.
criteria.upgrade_path: PIX4TEAM 1 owners can upgrade to the 2 for €499 ex VAT, cameras can be swapped as budgets allow up to 1.5 kg, and services can be added monthly [pix4team-01, pix4team-02]. Firmware updates are delivered through the apps. Whether upgrades continue depends on the reorganisation outcome [pix4team-05].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Film the same match with PIX4TEAM on a 4K camcorder and with a panoramic competitor, then compare the usable close-up detail for individual player review, which is where a real zoom wins [pix4team-01]. Test the app connection and field setup routine on your actual phone model, given the Samsung overlay complaints [pix4team-07]. Ask the company in writing how warranty and spare parts are guaranteed during the observation period [pix4team-06].

verdict.look_if: You run a US youth or amateur team, you already own or are willing to buy two GoPros, and you want automated full-game video delivered to YouTube for about $14 a game with no annual commitment [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-03]. You should also look if resolution matters, since dual 5K and 8K capture from current GoPros exceeds every fixed youth camera [seeusplay-02, seeusplay-06].
verdict.skip_if: You need live streaming, since the workflow is record, upload from SD cards, process in the cloud and deliver hours later [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05]. You should also skip it if you are in Europe or need a vendor with visible scale, since there is no European presence, the iOS app shows one rating, and the company discloses no funding, headcount or customer numbers [seeusplay-08, seeusplay-09, seeusplay-10].
watch_outs: There is no live streaming, and the vendor's own guidance is 15 minutes to a few hours of upload per 90-minute game followed by a processing turnaround of a few hours for 4K and 5K and up to eight hours for 8K [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06].

The terms grant SeeUsPlay an unrestricted, unlimited, irrevocable, perpetual, transferable, royalty-free licence over user contributions for promotional use and reserve the right to remove or disable files without notice [seeusplay-09].
Token expiry rules are not published in the FAQ or the terms, so ask before buying a 200-token pack [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-09].

The App Store seller is listed as SeeUssPlay LLC while the terms and Google Play name SeeUsPlay, Inc., and the Google Play listing shows 50+ downloads, so the customer base is small [seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11].
The current headline prices are labelled Spring Sale in September 2026, so treat the $349 and $599 token prices as promotional and the $399 and $699 figures as list [seeusplay-03].

Parents on a regional forum report no in-app preview and no recording indicator visible from behind the rig, and note the product lacks the event tagging and player tracking of Veo and Trace [seeusplay-12].

criteria.use_case_fit: SeeUsPlay covers soccer, American football including flag, rugby, baseball and softball, lacrosse, volleyball, basketball, field hockey and ice hockey, with soccer as the origin sport [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05, seeusplay-06]. It fits teams that want a full-game record and highlights for review and family viewing after the match [seeusplay-02]. It does not fit clubs that need live distribution or a coaching analysis layer [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-12].
criteria.capture_quality: Two GoPros on the rig capture 4K, 5K or 5.3K on HERO9 to HERO13 Black and up to 8K on the GoPro MISSION 1, and the cloud AI tracks from the raw full-resolution files [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-02, seeusplay-04]. Users can render several framing options per game, from no zoom to extra zoom, each as a separate video [seeusplay-06]. Parents describe the output as high quality with fairly reliable tracking [seeusplay-12].
criteria.automation_accuracy: Tracking is performed in the cloud on full-resolution footage, which gives the model more pixels than on-device systems, and baseball received sport-specific dynamic framing in June 2026 [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06]. Highlights are generated from events tagged by the user, there is no automatic event detection, and a parent notes the absence of auto tagging and player tracking compared with Veo and Trace [seeusplay-02, seeusplay-12]. No published accuracy figures exist.
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: The system is built on two side-by-side GoPros whose footage the cloud combines into a single tracked full-field output [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05]. Whether the output is a true stitched panorama or a virtual camera selecting between lenses is not documented. Not assessable further from public sources.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: There is no live streaming product, and delivery is measured in hours after the SD cards are uploaded [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05]. The June 2026 update reduced turnaround to a few hours for 4K and 5K and eight hours or less for 8K, with same-day delivery expected for most games [seeusplay-06].
criteria.reliability_resilience: Reliability rests on GoPro hardware, with two battery packs giving about 12 hours of runtime for a tournament weekend, and a 30-day money-back guarantee on purchases [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-07]. Recording is local to the SD cards, so venue connectivity does not affect capture [seeusplay-05]. Parents mention the lack of a rear recording indicator as a practical failure risk [seeusplay-12].
criteria.portability_install: The rig is a dual-camera mount on a tripod, with bundles from Just the Basics at $199 to Everything You Need at $499 on sale [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-03]. Setup is described as snapping two GoPros on, raising the tripod and tapping record in the app [seeusplay-05]. GoPros are bought separately, and the HERO8 and earlier, the HERO11 Mini and the HERO (2024) are unsupported [seeusplay-04].
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Upload happens from the SD cards after the game through the mobile app or the web app, and the vendor's guidance is 15 minutes to a few hours per 90-minute game depending on camera bitrate and connection [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06]. Dual 5K or 8K files are large, so a team without fast home or club broadband will feel the upload step [seeusplay-04].
criteria.workflow_ux: The three-step flow is record, create and share, with the app controlling both GoPros, the cloud building the full game and clips, and delivery direct to YouTube or download [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05]. June 2026 brought a web app for team management, scheduling, token balances and uploads, a rebuilt mobile app with custom zoom, unified login and public documentation at docs.seeusplay.com [seeusplay-06]. Parents report no in-app preview before upload [seeusplay-12].
criteria.analysis_layer: There is no analysis layer beyond user-tagged events that become highlights and an optional scoreboard overlay when scores are tagged [seeusplay-02, seeusplay-05]. Full-game downloads on every plan allow the file to go into any third-party analysis tool [seeusplay-04].
criteria.integrations: Delivery integrations are YouTube auto-upload to a team channel and Google Drive, both permitted only with the user's consent according to the privacy policy, plus direct download [seeusplay-05, seeusplay-13]. Sign-in supports Google, Facebook, Apple and email [seeusplay-06]. No league platform or analysis integrations are documented.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is outsourced to YouTube, which keeps SeeUsPlay out of the paywall and subscription business and means families watch on a channel the team controls [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-05]. There is no viewer app, no pay-per-view and no live feed [seeusplay-04].
criteria.data_access_ownership: Full game downloads are included on every plan with no paywall, so the team always holds a copy [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-04]. The terms grant SeeUsPlay an unrestricted, perpetual, transferable licence over user contributions for promotional use, place responsibility for transmitted data on the user and allow the company to remove or disable files without notice, and storage retention periods are not published [seeusplay-09]. Ownership of the underlying footage is not addressed in the FAQ [seeusplay-04].
criteria.privacy_compliance: The privacy policy, updated 16 June 2026, names SeeUsPlay, Inc., lists names, emails, club and team names and game information as collected data, states that the service does not knowingly market to children under 18 and requires parental consent for minors' accounts, and includes a section on legal bases that mirrors GDPR language [seeusplay-13]. The terms state the services are hosted in the United States and that international users consent to processing there [seeusplay-09]. The app store privacy labels list contact info and identifiers for analytics and functionality [seeusplay-10]. Facial recognition and biometrics are not mentioned [seeusplay-13].
criteria.security: Not assessable from public sources beyond the statements that YouTube and Google Drive access is used only for uploads and that the company keeps backups without liability for loss [seeusplay-09, seeusplay-13].
criteria.pricing_tco: Tokens cost $349 per 100 or $599 per 200 on the current sale, against list prices of $399 and $699, and a game costs 4 tokens in 4K, 5 in 5K and 10 in 8K, so a 100-token pack covers 25 games in 4K, 20 in 5K or 10 in 8K [seeusplay-03, seeusplay-04]. Rig bundles are $199 and $499 on sale, list $249 and $599, and GoPros are extra [seeusplay-03]. A team filming 25 games a season in 4K therefore spends about $349 in tokens plus a one-off rig and two cameras, with zero cost in the off-season, which the vendor itself puts at about $15 a game and half the price of subscription rivals [seeusplay-05, seeusplay-14]. YouTube upload and full downloads carry no extra charge [seeusplay-04].
criteria.support_service: Support is by email at support@seeusplay.com and a web form, with published setup, user and application guides since June 2026 and a 30-day money-back guarantee [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-06, seeusplay-07]. No phone support, SLA or reseller network is published.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: SeeUsPlay, Inc. is a private company with its registered developer address in Ashburn, Virginia and Virginia governing law, and it discloses no funding, revenue, headcount or customer numbers [seeusplay-09, seeusplay-11]. The product cadence is active, with multi-sport support in July 2025, 8K, baseball, a web app and a rebuilt mobile app in June 2026, and iOS updates through September 2026 [seeusplay-06, seeusplay-10, seeusplay-14]. Google Play shows 50+ downloads and the US App Store one rating, which points to a small base [seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11].
criteria.evidence_references: Primary evidence is the SeeUsPlay site, FAQ, how-it-works page, update blog, terms and privacy policy, plus the Apple and Google store listings [seeusplay-01, seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05, seeusplay-06, seeusplay-09, seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11, seeusplay-13]. Third-party evidence is one DC Urban Moms parent thread from March 2025 [seeusplay-12]. No press coverage, funding record or independent review was found.
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: A parent with a season of use reports high-quality video, fairly reliable tracking and no buyer's regret, while noting the missing preview, the hidden recording indicator and the absence of auto tagging and player tracking [seeusplay-12]. Store ratings are too few to be meaningful [seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11].
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: SeeUsPlay is a pure cloud production model, with dumb capture on GoPros and all tracking, framing and rendering done after upload [seeusplay-04, seeusplay-05]. This gives it resolution headroom and lets it adopt new GoPro models quickly, at the cost of delivery latency and upload burden [seeusplay-06].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The apps are in English on iOS and Android, and the web app runs in a desktop browser [seeusplay-06, seeusplay-10, seeusplay-11]. No other languages or European storefront pricing are published.
criteria.upgrade_path: Upgrades come from buying newer GoPros, since the same rig and tokens work across HERO9 to MISSION 1, and from choosing higher resolutions at more tokens per game [seeusplay-02, seeusplay-04]. There is no path into live streaming or analysis from the same vendor [seeusplay-04].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the per-game token economics against your actual season length, since zero off-season cost is the core pitch [seeusplay-03, seeusplay-05]. Test the SD-card upload time from a typical club connection for a dual 5K game, since that is the workflow's weak point [seeusplay-04]. Test the 8K MISSION 1 output at extra zoom on a full-size pitch to see whether the resolution headroom translates into usable close framing [seeusplay-06].

free.why: Trace exists because its founders, who started with the AlpineReplay ski tracking app in 2010, realised the person who will pay for youth sports video is the parent, so they gave the camera away and sold the child's highlights [trace-03, trace-01]. verdict.look_if: You are a US club or state association that wants every team filmed with no capital outlay and you are comfortable with families paying per player for the value [trace-01, trace-08]. You want automatic per player highlight reels and a recruiting profile more than you want a tactical analysis suite [trace-05, trace-11].
verdict.skip_if: You are in Europe or Italy, since Trace sells in US dollars, ships from a US warehouse and offers no EU pricing or support [trace-01, trace-05]. You need full match downloads for coaching without buying several Pro subscriptions, or you need processed video the same evening, because processing can take up to 12 hours after an upload that itself takes hours on a normal connection [trace-06, trace-11].
watch_outs: Trustpilot shows a 1.6 out of 5 score from 24 reviews, 96% of them one star, with automatic renewals, a seven day refund window, email only support and full game downloads gated behind additional Pro subscriptions as the recurring themes [trace-04].
A typical match produces about 16 GB of data and takes 3 hours 49 minutes to upload on a 10 Mbps line over ethernet, then up to 12 hours of processing, so same day review is not realistic [trace-06].
The livestream is a fixed wide shot with no panning or zooming, needs a hotspot left under the camera and consumes about 50% more battery per 90 minute game [trace-07].
The free camera is a lease that remains Trace property, with a USD 99 fee if you pay monthly, so leaving the service means returning hardware [trace-01].
The privacy policy is dated July 2018, references only California law, states that uploaded content becomes publicly available and makes no mention of GDPR [trace-12].

criteria.use_case_fit: Trace is a parent product first, delivering AI edited highlights of one named player identified by jersey colour and number, with the team's full game and tactical highlights available on top [trace-01, trace-11]. It supports soccer, basketball and American football and its reference logos are US youth clubs such as De Anza Force and Legends FC [trace-05]. Club plans exist for full game downloads and are priced on request [trace-11].
criteria.capture_quality: Trace states its camera shoots in 1080p with a computational capture engine for smooth panning and stability, mounted midfield on a 16 foot tripod with sandbags [trace-09, trace-01]. The pricing page describes 180 degree field coverage and the PlayerCam view applies a 4x digital zoom on the tracked player [trace-01]. No sensor, frame rate or low light specification is published.
criteria.automation_accuracy: Player identification relies on jersey colours and the player's number plus what Trace calls hundreds of other signals, with no face recognition mentioned [trace-11]. Trustpilot reviewers describe glitchy software and poor AI tracking, and Trace's own copy claims over a million highlights captured weekly from thousands of games [trace-04, trace-08]. No independent accuracy figure exists.
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: One camera provides the wide TraceCam view and the software derives the PlayerCam crop, while MultiCam lets parents add smartphone angles that are synced to the main recording [trace-05]. There is no multi camera stitching of the pitch itself.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Livestreaming is a beta feature that sends a fixed, unpanned wide shot over a hotspot placed under the camera, using about 700 MB an hour at the highest setting, and viewers need only a free Trace account [trace-07]. Delay is not published. Live updates such as score notifications exist alongside the stream [trace-05].
criteria.reliability_resilience: Trace warns that lowering the camera during a game loses the recording and that livestreaming adds roughly 50% battery drain per game [trace-07]. Reviewers in 2026 report cameras that failed activation and an app that blocked recording over a payment dispute [trace-04]. The tripod kit weighs under 10 lbs and sets up in about 15 minutes [trace-11].
criteria.portability_install: The kit is a collapsible 16 foot tripod with three sandbags and a camera, carried to the field and positioned at midfield by a parent or manager [trace-01, trace-11]. It is fully portable with no venue installation, which suits travel teams and multi field complexes.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Upload is by ethernet cable to a home router, with a 16 GB match taking almost four hours on 10 Mbps and a 5 Mbps minimum recommended [trace-06]. Livestreaming needs a WPA2 hotspot and does not work on enterprise or captive portal networks [trace-07]. There is no built in cellular modem.
criteria.workflow_ux: A manager sets jersey colours and numbers in the Teams app, presses record from the phone, then plugs the camera in at home and waits for an email when highlights are ready [trace-11]. Pro subscribers can download and edit highlights, create playlists and see PlayerFocus Analytics, while Basic subscribers see only the last five games [trace-01]. Support is by email through a help centre with no phone line, according to reviewers [trace-04].
criteria.analysis_layer: PlayerFocus Analytics offers possession tracking and auto tagged plays and full game tactical highlights are included in both plans [trace-01, trace-05]. There are no drawing tools, custom tagging boards or fitness data, so coaches wanting analysis depth will pair it with another tool.
criteria.integrations: Trace iD provides a public shareable profile aimed at recruiters and custom downloads cropped for social platforms [trace-09, trace-10]. State association partnerships with US Youth Soccer, Florida and Eastern Pennsylvania are commercial agreements with no data integration described [trace-13, trace-08]. No public API is documented.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is limited to shared livestream links, the Trace app and Trace iD profiles, with no white label OTT, paywall or advertising layer [trace-07, trace-09]. This is a family sharing product with no broadcast platform behind it.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Basic subscribers keep access to the last five games only and Pro subscribers to all games while subscribed [trace-01]. Full game downloads require a Club plan or enough family Pro subscriptions, a limit a September 2026 reviewer described as six extra paid subscriptions [trace-11, trace-04]. The privacy policy says the company may keep a copy of unrevised information after edits and that uploaded content becomes publicly available [trace-12].
criteria.privacy_compliance: The privacy policy is dated 12 July 2018, references CCPA only, says the company does not knowingly collect data from children under 13 unless a parent is involved and does not mention GDPR or data location [trace-12]. Player identification uses jersey number and Trace makes no mention of face recognition [trace-11]. No blurring, opt out or consent workflow for opposing team players is described anywhere, which matters because every recording includes the other team's children.
criteria.pricing_tco: A family pays USD 180 a year for Basic or USD 300 a year for Pro, or USD 25 and USD 40 a month, and the camera lease worth USD 795 is free on annual billing or USD 99 one off on monthly billing [trace-01]. A team of 15 families on Pro costs USD 4,500 a year in total, which Reeplayer's comparison puts at USD 7,295 over three years, so the model moves the cost from the club to the parents and the total stays high [trace-14]. Cancellation disputes and a seven day refund window are the main cost surprises reported [trace-04].
criteria.support_service: Support runs through support.traceup.com and email, and Trustpilot reviewers in January 2026 complained there is no live agent or phone support [trace-05, trace-04]. Hardware ships from a US warehouse within about three days [trace-09]. Warranty covers manufacturer defects on the leased kit [trace-01].
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Trace raised a USD 47 million Series C in April 2022 at a USD 190 million valuation led by Pelion Venture Partners, bringing total funding to USD 65.2 million, on 2021 revenue above USD 10 million [trace-03]. Crunchbase now lists the company in Austin with 51 to 100 employees, down from about 100 with a plan for 160 to 170 in 2022 [trace-02, trace-03]. The 2026 strategy is free camera deals through state associations such as Florida and Eastern Pennsylvania [trace-08].
criteria.evidence_references: Named partners include US Youth Soccer since October 2020, Florida Youth Soccer and Eastern Pennsylvania Youth Soccer in 2026 and clubs such as De Anza Force, Legends FC and Sound FC on the homepage [trace-13, trace-08, trace-05]. Forbes reported over 1,000 clubs and 1.4 million athletes with camera access in April 2022 [trace-03].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Public sentiment comes almost entirely from parents and it is poor on Trustpilot, at 1.6 out of 5, with praise limited to the camera and tripod hardware [trace-04]. The App Store and club testimonials on Trace's own site present a more positive picture, and no independent coach survey exists.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: The camera records locally and all AI processing happens in the cloud after upload, which is why a match needs 16 GB of upload and up to 12 hours of processing [trace-06]. Livestreaming bypasses this with a direct fixed feed from the camera over a hotspot [trace-07].
criteria.accessibility_languages: The website, apps and help centre are in English and pricing is in US dollars only [trace-01, trace-05]. No other languages or accessibility features are documented.
criteria.upgrade_path: Families move from Basic to Pro for full history, analytics, downloads and four family emails, and clubs move to a Club plan for full game downloads [trace-01, trace-11]. The camera is the same at every tier and Trace states renewals include free hardware renewal [trace-01].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test the per player highlight reel against a player who changes position or shares a jersey colour with the opposition, since identification is jersey based [trace-11]. Time the full upload and processing cycle on your own connection against Trace's 16 GB and 12 hour figures [trace-06]. Read the cancellation and download terms before the season starts, because those two points generate most of the public complaints [trace-04].

verdict.look_if: You want to own a tracking camera for under EUR 1,000 with no recurring fee and you record mostly for parents, highlights and social clips, with professional analysis a secondary need [xbotgo-02, xbotgo-11]. You are in a market the company ships to directly, including the EU, and you can live with SD card and app based workflows [xbotgo-10].
verdict.skip_if: You need a club system where footage lands in a shared analysis platform automatically, since XbotGo's cloud is 20 GB and the analysis add on is priced per match with a 24 hour turnaround [xbotgo-02, xbotgo-12]. You need clear answers on data residency and the processing entity, because the iOS app is published by a Nanjing company and the privacy documentation does not address European data location [xbotgo-14].
watch_outs: Falcon specifications differ between the September 2025 Kickstarter press release (10,000 mAh, IP55, 180 degree tilt) and the March 2026 general sale release (9,600 mAh, IPX5, 160 degree tilt), so confirm the shipping unit's rating before relying on weather resistance [xbotgo-07, xbotgo-06].
The Falcon launched at USD 699 in March 2026 and is listed at USD 799 in September 2026, a 14% rise in six months [xbotgo-06, xbotgo-02].

The company describes itself as Silicon Valley based and the Kickstarter creator location is Mountain View, while the September 2025 press release carried a Dallas dateline and the company recruits in Dallas, so the operating base is ambiguous [xbotgo-08, xbotgo-04, xbotgo-07].
The iOS app developer of record is 深眸远智(南京)信息科技有限公司, a Nanjing company, and App Store reviewers report tracking drift in second halves and persistent Bluetooth disconnects [xbotgo-14].
A September 2026 Trustpilot reviewer states a replacement part was offered only in exchange for a positive review, which should temper the 4.4 Trustpilot score [xbotgo-09].

criteria.use_case_fit: XbotGo targets parents and coaches across more than 20 team sports with two products, a phone gimbal and a standalone camera, and the Pro Soccer analysis add on launched in September 2026 moves it toward coaching use in football [xbotgo-03, xbotgo-12, xbotgo-13]. Cal South uses it in coaching education and Olympic Development Program evaluations, which is the most club like reference on record [xbotgo-15]. It is a per team consumer purchase, with no venue or federation offer.
criteria.capture_quality: Falcon records native 4K at 30 fps or 1080p at 60 fps from a dual camera unit with a Sony IMX678 1/1.8 inch sensor and a secondary GC4663 sensor, with 360 degree pan and no stitching or cropping claimed [xbotgo-01, xbotgo-07]. Chameleon output depends on the phone, up to 4K 60 fps on iPhone and selected Samsung models [xbotgo-03]. A Trustpilot reviewer describes the Falcon picture as a night and day improvement over previous cameras [xbotgo-09].
criteria.automation_accuracy: Falcon uses a 6 TOPS on device AI processor with sport specific tracking logic, zone mapping and auto zoom [xbotgo-06, xbotgo-01]. Users report only a handful of missed plays in a 7v7 game and weaker ball tracking on set pieces and long passes, and App Store reviews describe drift in the second half and confusion from sideline staff [xbotgo-09, xbotgo-14]. Basketball has jersey number recognition on Chameleon and soccer tracking is described as the weaker sport [xbotgo-03, xbotgo-14].
criteria.multi_angle_stitching: Falcon combines a wide sensor and a tracking sensor in one housing and XbotGo states it does not stitch, so there is a single broadcast style output [xbotgo-01]. There is no multi camera pitch coverage.
criteria.latency_live_readiness: Both products offer one tap livestreaming in the app and RTMP output to third party platforms at no extra charge [xbotgo-01, xbotgo-06]. The camera has WiFi 6 and BLE 5.2 and no cellular modem, so the live feed depends on a phone hotspot or venue WiFi [xbotgo-01]. Stream latency is not published.
criteria.reliability_resilience: Falcon runs about four hours per charge with a three hour USB C recharge, stores to microSD up to 1 TB and is rated IPX5 or IP55 depending on the document [xbotgo-01, xbotgo-06, xbotgo-07]. The stated operating ceiling is 39.6 degrees Celsius, which matters for southern European summer fixtures [xbotgo-07]. App Store reviewers cite Bluetooth disconnects as a recurring issue [xbotgo-14].
criteria.portability_install: Both units are tripod mounted on a standard quarter inch thread with no installation, and XbotGo sells NT4 steel and carbon tripods and a weather umbrella as accessories [xbotgo-02, xbotgo-07]. This is the most portable class in the market alongside Trace and Veo portable cameras.
criteria.connectivity_bandwidth: Recording is local to microSD, uploads go to XbotGo cloud over WiFi through the app, and livestream needs a hotspot or venue WiFi over WiFi 6 [xbotgo-01]. No bandwidth figures are published. There is no built in SIM.
criteria.workflow_ux: The user maps the zone in the app, starts recording and later uploads to the cloud for team sharing and AI highlights [xbotgo-01]. The iOS app is rated 4.5 from about 1,500 ratings with praise for ease of use and complaints about connectivity and support follow through [xbotgo-14]. Pro Soccer analysis is ordered per match from the Gallery in app version 5.0 or later [xbotgo-12].
criteria.analysis_layer: Pro Soccer, launched September 2026, produces goals, shots, corners and saves highlights, attack and defence statistics and a one page tactical report within 24 hours for USD 15 per match at promotional pricing and USD 23.99 at list, with one credit per team per video [xbotgo-12, xbotgo-13, xbotgo-16]. It requires continuous footage under 130 minutes uploaded to XbotGo cloud and numbered jerseys in different colours [xbotgo-16]. An early reviewer called the output borderline useless with long processing, so treat it as version one [xbotgo-09].
criteria.integrations: RTMP livestream output is the only documented integration [xbotgo-01]. There is no documented API, no export to third party analysis platforms and no federation database connection.
criteria.distribution_ott: Distribution is limited to shared cloud videos, highlights for social media and RTMP streams to platforms such as YouTube [xbotgo-01, xbotgo-06]. There is no paywall, subscription or advertising layer for clubs.
criteria.data_access_ownership: Footage stays on the user's microSD card and the user chooses what to upload, which is the strongest ownership position in this group [xbotgo-01]. Cloud storage is 20 GB free and Pro Soccer results are stored indefinitely at no charge [xbotgo-06, xbotgo-16]. Retention terms for uploaded video beyond the 20 GB allowance are not published.
criteria.privacy_compliance: XbotGo publishes no blurring, opt out or consent tooling and its materials do not discuss minors, GDPR or data residency [xbotgo-01, xbotgo-08]. The iOS app publisher is a Nanjing entity while the company presents itself as a Silicon Valley brand, so European clubs should ask where cloud video is processed before uploading footage of children [xbotgo-14, xbotgo-08]. Local recording without upload remains a workable privacy posture.
criteria.pricing_tco: Falcon costs USD 799 or EUR 869 for the camera alone, USD 969 or EUR 1,049 with a steel tripod and USD 1,029 or EUR 1,119 with a carbon tripod, plus a microSD card, and Chameleon costs USD 299.99 or EUR 329.99 with bundles to USD 549.99 [xbotgo-02, xbotgo-11, xbotgo-03]. There is no subscription for tracking, livestream or 20 GB of cloud, so three year cost for a Falcon is the purchase price plus any analysis at USD 15 to 23.99 per match [xbotgo-06, xbotgo-12]. Cal South members receive a 20% discount [xbotgo-15].
criteria.support_service: Support is by phone on a US toll free number from 8 am to 6 pm Eastern seven days a week and by email, with a one year warranty and 30 day free returns [xbotgo-08, xbotgo-02]. XbotGo answers 91% of negative Trustpilot reviews within about a week, and App Store reviewers report mixed outcomes on hardware exchanges [xbotgo-09, xbotgo-14]. European support hours and a European return address are not published.
criteria.company_health_roadmap: Blink Tech, Inc. trades as XbotGo, was founded by David Tan and funded the Falcon through a Kickstarter that closed at USD 2,548,287 from 5,099 backers on 17 October 2025 after an earlier USD 300,000 Chameleon campaign [xbotgo-04, xbotgo-05]. The company claims over 203,000 active members, 500 plus teams and customers in 100 plus countries, and launched Pro Soccer at IFA Berlin in September 2026 [xbotgo-08, xbotgo-13]. Venture funding and revenue are not disclosed.
criteria.evidence_references: Cal South, the Southern California state association, renewed XbotGo as official AI camera partner in December 2025 with use in coaching education and ODP [xbotgo-15]. Kickstarter backers and Trustpilot reviewers provide the bulk of user evidence, and no European club reference was found [xbotgo-04, xbotgo-09].
criteria.coach_analyst_satisfaction: Trustpilot shows 4.4 out of 5 from 155 reviews with 76% five star and 13% one star, praising picture quality and support and criticising set piece tracking and the analysis output [xbotgo-09]. The App Store rating is 4.5 from about 1,500 ratings [xbotgo-14]. No analyst or club review is public, so all of this sentiment comes from parents.
criteria.edge_vs_cloud: Tracking runs on the camera's 6 TOPS processor at the edge, highlights and Pro Soccer analysis run in XbotGo's cloud after upload [xbotgo-06, xbotgo-16]. Cloud location is not published.
criteria.accessibility_languages: The store serves more than 40 regions with local currencies and the site is in English, with warehouses in the US, Canada, Australia, the UK and Germany [xbotgo-02, xbotgo-10]. App language support is not documented.
criteria.upgrade_path: Users move from the Chameleon phone gimbal to the standalone Falcon and add Pro Soccer analysis per match without a subscription [xbotgo-03, xbotgo-12]. XbotGo states cloud sharing works across both devices [xbotgo-01].
criteria.differentiators_worth_testing: Test native 4K tracking from a single unit against a stitched panoramic camera on the same match, since XbotGo's claim is broadcast style framing without cropping [xbotgo-01]. Test Pro Soccer on a youth match with similar kit colours to see how often the credit is refunded for a rejected video [xbotgo-16]. Test the livestream over a phone hotspot for a full 90 minutes with battery monitoring [xbotgo-01].

free.one_line: LiveBarn is a North American subscription network of fixed cameras installed free in more than 4,000 rinks, courts and fields, sold to families at $26.95 or $36.95 a month, and bought by GTCR for more than $400 million in April 2026 [livebarn-01, livebarn-02, livebarn-03].

Venues join because the install and operation cost them nothing [livebarn-04].
free.why: LiveBarn exists because indoor venues host thousands of games a week that nobody films, so it took the capital cost of fixed cameras onto its own balance sheet and sold the output as a Netflix-style subscription [livebarn-01, livebarn-04]. It matters now because the April 2026 sale to GTCR at more than $400 million, on estimated revenue of about $80 million, is the largest valuation marker yet for automated youth match video and GTCR has said it will expand from hockey into soccer, basketball, volleyball, baseball and swimming through its new Ascent Sports Group [livebarn-02, livebarn-03, livebarn-05]. It tells you that the venue-network subscription model, where the platform owns cameras and viewers and the club owns nothing, is what private equity is paying for, and that Europe has no equivalent at this scale [livebarn-01, livebarn-02].

free.name: Sics (SICS S.r.l., Soccerment Group)
free.payer_model_label: Club pays for a coaching tool
free.one_line: Sics is the Bassano del Grappa match analysis house behind VideoMatch and LiveTag, used by Serie A staffs since 1995, now part of Soccerment Group and sold to amateur coaches from EUR 80 a month with Veo Cam 3 as its recommended automatic camera [sics-01, sics-02, sics-03].
free.who_for: Italian professional and semi-professional technical staffs first, and since the Personal edition, amateur and youth coaches who want the same tagging, playlist and drawing tools on footage from a Veo or any other camera [sics-02, sics-03]. It suits clubs that treat the camera as an input and want an Italian-language analysis workflow with local support [sics-01, sics-04].
free.why: Sics exists because Italian coaching culture wanted detailed video tagging before automated cameras existed, and the company built a 30-year client list from Inter to the Italian federation on that demand [sics-01]. It matters now because Soccerment absorbed it in 2025 with Azimut Libera Impresa money, launched SICS Atlas in August 2026 as an AI-native platform, and positions Veo as the capture front end, which makes Sics the analysis layer most likely to sit on top of automated match video in Italy [sics-03, sics-04, sics-05]. It tells you that in Italy the analysis software vendor, with EUR 1.1 million revenue and seven staff, is a small but strategically placed node that every camera vendor selling into Italian clubs will need to integrate with [sics-05, sics-06].

free.one_line: Joymo is a Norwegian OTT platform for grassroots and federation sport that lets clubs stream from a phone, encoder or camera and sell access to viewers with safeguarding controls built in [joymo-01, joymo-02].

free.name: Min Fotboll (Svenska Fotbollförbundet)
free.payer_model_label: Distribution layer, club and viewer split
free.one_line: Min Fotboll is the Swedish FA's official app, in which volunteers stream matches from a phone or a connected Veo or Spiideo camera and viewers pay SEK 59 for 30 days of every youth match in Sweden, with half the revenue after VAT going to a club of the viewer's choice [minfotboll-01, minfotboll-02].
free.who_for: Every Swedish club, from children's teams to lower senior divisions, since the app is free to use, tied to the FA's competition database and the only place SvFF sanctions youth streaming [minfotboll-01, minfotboll-03]. Families and grandparents who want to follow a child's team anywhere in the country are the paying audience [minfotboll-01].
free.why: Min Fotboll exists because the Swedish FA decided that grassroots streaming, sponsorship and communication should sit inside one federation-owned app, away from fragmented commercial platforms, and it framed GDPR control as a reason from the start [minfotboll-03, minfotboll-04]. It matters now because it is the clearest example of a federation owning the distribution and checkout layer and treating camera vendors such as Veo and Spiideo as interchangeable inputs, with nearly 11,500 livestreams and 126,000 matches with user content in 2024 [minfotboll-01, minfotboll-05]. It tells you that where a federation moves first, the automated camera becomes a peripheral and the pricing power moves to the app that holds the fixtures [minfotboll-02, minfotboll-06].
free.price_band: Free for clubs; youth viewer pass SEK 59 per 30 days for all youth matches; senior PPV set by the club; club replay package SEK 2,000 per year; 50 percent of revenue after VAT to the chosen club

italy.note: Min Fotboll is a Swedish federation service available only for Swedish competitions and has no presence outside Sweden [minfotboll-01, minfotboll-03].

free.name: Solidsport
free.payer_model_label: Distribution layer, club and viewer split
free.one_line: Solidsport is a Swedish streaming platform that lets clubs, leagues and federations broadcast matches from any camera, including Veo, and sell them to viewers on a 50/50 revenue split after VAT [solidsport-01, solidsport-02].
free.who_for: Clubs and federations in the Nordics, Germany and Austria that want a free-to-join channel with pay-per-view, season passes and supporter subscriptions and are willing to trade half the gross for a turnkey platform [solidsport-01, solidsport-03]. free.why: Solidsport exists because grassroots clubs had cameras and audiences but no way to charge for a stream, so it built a channel platform that costs the club nothing upfront and splits the gross [solidsport-01, solidsport-02]. It matters now because federation-wide deals such as SHFV in June 2025 and the Swedish Handball extension in September 2025 turn it into the default distribution layer that camera vendors plug into, and revenue grew 42 percent to SEK 85 million in 2025 on that model [solidsport-03, solidsport-05, solidsport-06]. It tells you that in Europe the money in automated match video is being made by whoever owns the checkout page, and that camera vendors without a monetisation layer end up as suppliers to platforms like this one [solidsport-04, solidsport-07].
